title: Heating Required
loc: Birkenhead (Merseyside) - 1960s office block on the former Cammell Laird shipyard
desc: A paranormal investigation group was called into this building after staff reported certain areas as always being cold, and fleeting shapes could be spotted out of the corner of one's eyes.

title: Maid
loc: Birkenhead (Merseyside) - Area of former Birkenhead Hall (no longer standing), Pouton Road
desc: This pretty maid was murdered by her jealous mistress, who was convinced the maid was having an affair with the master of the hall. It was not the case, and the little maid now haunts the former grounds. The phantom has taken to being mistaken for a hitchhiker along the nearby road.

title: Face at the Windows
loc: Birkenhead (Merseyside) - Car park on the corner of Argyle Street and Canning Street opposite the Cheshire Lines building
desc: This phantom is said to peer into windows of stationary vehicles in this car park. On the site once stood a factory, reputedly haunted by the ghost of a woman who hanged herself there.

title: Little Old Lady
desc: Lights turn themselves on and off, doors open and close, and a handful of staff have reported seeing a strange old lady walking around the site. Men in boiler suits have been watched walking past windows only to vanish shortly after.

title: Woman
loc: Birkenhead (Merseyside) - Private residence close to the A552
desc: Prior to renovation, a ghostly woman would be seen in the house.

title: Edwardian Woman
loc: Birkenhead (Merseyside) - Private residence near Borough Road
desc: A witness reported repeatedly seeing a woman wearing Edwardian clothing in their home, although the encounters were not fearful.

title: Edwardians
desc: Dressed in Edwardian attire, a man and woman were seen in one top floor bedroom. Both seemed to be gentle with no hint of malice, and interacted with children in the house. Other people in Edwardian clothing would be seen out of the corner of the eye on the top floor.

title: Older Lady
desc: Dressed in black and wearing a bonnet, an older lady would be briefly seen along this road before suddenly vanishing. A newspaper reported cyclists had to break sharply to avoid hitting her. Other witnesses spotted a small ball of fire which quickly disappeared.

title: John Bibby
desc: Seen once a year, Bibby rides his coach with his decapitated head in his lap.

title: Grey Lady
loc: Ince Blundell (Merseyside) - A565 through Ince Woods
date: Unknown, but said to be at midnight on an unstated date
desc: This phantom woman will manifest close to a round house, in front of oncoming traffic and causing vehicles to crash. It is unclear whether the ghost is a continuation of the haunting along Park Wall Road.

title: Grey Lady
loc: Ince Blundell (Merseyside) - White cross along Park Wall Road
desc: Possibly also known as the Pink Lady, this woman had an affair with a local landowner and took her own life when she fell pregnant.

title: Giant
desc: A figure standing eight feet tall with a black beard and a scowling face would appear at night and declare, 'I am the ghost of the giant of Hale!' before disappearing.

title: Pacing
desc: It was reported in the local press during the 1970s that footsteps could be heard within this building coming from empty rooms, although a former worker at the site said that the story was a publicity stunt.

title: Old Woman
loc: Liverpool (Merseyside) - 82 Wimborne Road, Huyton (house no longer standing)
desc: A family living here were terrified by a phantom old lady who stood five-foot tall, bent over with a walking stick. Her face was little more than a shrivelled skull. Builders working close to the site quit once they heard an exorcism had taken place. The house has since been demolished.

title: Small Woman
loc: Liverpool (Merseyside) - 9 and 11 South Hunter Street (houses demolished in early 1960s)
desc: Seen by a mother and daughter on separate occasions, this phantom was described as a small woman wearing a lace cap and soft shawl. She was semi-transparent and vanished when approached.

title: George
desc: George has been seen several times standing by beds on the fifth floor.

title: Glowing Ball
desc: The hall is reputedly haunted by former residents and ghost hunts on the site have turned up flashes of light and sightings of glowing balls. An 'orb' caught on camera featured in the press in 2014.

title: The Sarge
loc: Liverpool (Merseyside) - Ambulance training centre, Quarry Street, Woolton
desc: For many years the building was reputedly haunted by an entity known as 'The Sarge' - a former policeman killed when the wheel of his patrol wagon struck a bollard and he was thrown to the ground. Ambulance crews reported phantom footsteps, breaking windows and doors which unlocked and opened themselves.

title: Flag Waver
loc: Liverpool (Merseyside) - Area around former Otterspool rail station
desc: Before closing in 1951, a teenager was saved by a man from being hit by a train, although the rescuer was killed in the process. He is said to wave a red warning flag in the area.

title: Smells and Shadows
loc: Liverpool (Merseyside) - Battle of the Atlantic Bunker
desc: A visitor to the site could smell perfume where a Wren had fallen to her death, spotted strange shadows, and experienced the sensation of being followed. When the witness returned years later, the location had changed and they experienced nothing untoward, although stories tell of figures in naval uniform who walk through walls.

title: Time Slip
desc: On various dates, several people (including an off duty policeman) have reported slipping back in time along this road, finding them surrounded by people dressed in clothing of the 1940s, with a cobbled street and old style shops.

title: Spookside
desc: It was reported in the local press that the cast of 'The Close', a low budget British horror film being filmed at the former soap opera site, regarded the set as haunted. Lights would flicker out at inopportune moments, items would disappear, and the final scene of the film was constantly cancelled as bad weather would come from nowhere.

title: George
loc: Liverpool (Merseyside) - Coach and Horses public house
desc: A former landlord, George still returns to keep a watchful eye on his former establishment.

title: Earl of Sefton
date: Late twentieth century, camera in April 2009, most recently July 2013
desc: The Sixth Earl of Sefton has been sighted walking through the tearoom and in his former bedroom. An incorporeal young boy was once seen standing by the fireplace in the dining room, while other strange shadows have been reported drifting down various corridors. Footage from a CCTV camera in April 2009 reputedly shows a phantom figure moving across the grounds, though the image is more likely to be a close-up of an insect. Two people exploring the basement in 2013 encountered a short hideous figure in a cloak, before later spotting the figure on the staircase where he vanished.

title: Gin Runner
loc: Liverpool (Merseyside) - David Lewis Northern Hospital (closed 1978 and demolished)
desc: Beaten to death nearby by Customs officers who caught the man trying to bring his illicit goods ashore, the ghost of the smuggler was reported in the hospital that was built close to the site of his murder. The site also had the reputation as being haunted by Nurse Jones, murdered at the site in 1919.

title: Spring Healed Jack
desc: This area was one from which this enigmatic creature/entity was reported.

title: Murdered Woman
loc: Liverpool (Merseyside) - Former hotel along Sir Thomas Street
desc: A voice in an empty toilet was heard issuing warnings of future events, while a figure was seen passing a door and climbing the stairs when the three people in the building were accounted for. A local legend says that a woman was murdered on the staircase close to the toilets.

title: Footsteps
loc: Liverpool (Merseyside) - Former police and fire station, Lark Lane
desc: Footsteps have been reported on the rear staircase and a heavy door opens and closes unaided, according to the Night Vision Investigations team.

title: Older Woman
loc: Liverpool (Merseyside) - Former post office (currently a computer centre)
desc: A woman in a checked red coat walked by two witnesses who were standing by a telephone box. The woman passed within thirty centimetres of the pair and proceeded to walk through the locked door to the post office.

title: Flying Glasses
loc: Liverpool (Merseyside) - Head of Steam public house, Lime Street
desc: Glasses are said to be thrown from shelves and people feel something following them upstairs.

title: Baby Bouncer
loc: Liverpool (Merseyside) - House owned by Liverpool Housing Trust, Madryn Street, Toxteth
desc: A family living here with a poltergeist reported that the entity picked up their young son and threw him from his cot. The entity would also move the washing machine around the kitchen, hide money, and smash ashtrays.

title: Purple Faced Girl
loc: Liverpool (Merseyside) - Huyton, streets in the area
desc: One local myth says certain streets were home to a blue/purple faced young girl who would follow families with children.

title: Lady in Blue
loc: Liverpool (Merseyside) - Jessie Appleton's public house (aka The Dingle) (no longer operating), Park Road
desc: Vicky Lee appeared in the press claiming her pub was haunted, having experienced footsteps in locked areas and unexplained breezes across the neck. Vicky's son encountered an older woman wearing a blue dress who vanished from a room.

title: Monk
loc: Liverpool (Merseyside) - Knowsley Hall and Riding Hill
desc: A phantom monk is said to haunt the area around the hall and the hill. A local legend says a secret tunnel ran from the monastery that once stood on the hill, and that the path the ghostly monk takes indicates the route of the passage.

title: Swinging Swain
loc: Liverpool (Merseyside) - Lea Hall (or possibly Lee Hall) (no longer standing), Gateacre
desc: A local villager who tried his luck with the squire's daughter found himself lynched from a tree close to the hall. On windy nights, the body could be heard swinging. A murder in the hall itself could be repeatedly heard, the moans of a woman and the laughter of her homicidal husband. A journalist who visited the hall between the world wars looking for ghosts to write about found himself frozen to the spot, surrounded by complete silence; he managed to escape and flee after hearing a clock striking in the distance.

title: Floating Torso
desc: Sightings of the ghost of Lime Street are said to go back hundreds or years. One of the more recent witnesses described the entity as being quite tall, though the legs could not be seen, with the mouth silently moving. An unnamed hotel (that later became offices) along the road is also haunted by the figure of a tall woman.

title: Thomas Campbell Black
loc: Liverpool (Merseyside) - Liverpool Airport, formerly known as Speke
desc: Black died in an accident on the runway of the airfield in 1936 - his shadowy form has been seen walking around the area where the old hangars stood.

title: Hitchhiker
desc: Killed in the middle of the twentieth century in the tunnel under the Mersey, this phantom hitchhiker is still occasionally seen.

title: The Demons Below See
desc: This old well has the words 'Qui non dat quod habet, Daemon infra vide 1414' carved above it. It was said that any traveller passing by would have no choice but to drink the waters and give a donation to charity, otherwise the Devil (chained under the well) would laugh.

title: Coal Thrower
loc: Liverpool (Merseyside) - Myers Street, Smithdown Lane (no longer exists)
desc: Many of the windows along this street were broken by thrown pieces of coal. The breakages continued after police began patrolling the area.

title: Voices
desc: A team of French film makers reportedly encountered children's voices, and a strange white mist while at this site. The former hospital grounds has a reputation for being haunted by a small child on the top floor, while dragging sounds have been reported elsewhere and small items associated with childhood thrown around.

title: Screeching Ginny
loc: Liverpool (Merseyside) - Old Garston Dock Station, and St Mary's Road, Garston
desc: The local witch known as Screeching Ginny appeared and gave chase to a group of school children who were playing on the disused tracks of the railway station. Folklore says the witch fell in love with a local boy but it was unrequited; as the boy left the area with his girlfriend on a train, Ginny threw herself on the tracks and died. Although the station is long gone, the witch still haunts the area.

title: Cloaked Figure
desc: A firefighter tackling a blaze in the former rectory believed he spotted a figure standing by the engine, although no one was there at the time. The building had a reputation as being haunted by the ghost of a cloaked figure.

title: Screaming Woman
desc: Two students sought help from a medium after enduring a phantom woman in her fifties who would scream during the night and call out the name 'Shelley Jones'. On one occasion the students returned to find the message 'get out' written out on the floor using their socks.

title: Upstairs Bangs
loc: Liverpool (Merseyside) - Private house along Sackville Street
desc: The upper part of the building was subjected to multiple bangs and crashes with no apparent source - the entity was also blamed for pushing a woman down the stairs, causing injuries that required hospital treatment.

title: Man
loc: Liverpool (Merseyside) - Private residence (likely no longer standing)
desc: An occupant observed a ghostly man standing on the scullery floor, the sight unnerving the witness to such an extent that the area was avoided. The floor would later collapse, revealing a hidden well where the figure had stood.

title: Murdered Man?
loc: Liverpool (Merseyside) - Private residence (likely no longer standing), Toxteth Park
desc: A court case revolved around a maid suing her employer for a month's salary having left her job after encountering a ghost. The maid stated the ghost had not unduly worried her, but stories about bodies being buried under the building had done so. The judge suggested that her former employer pay the outstanding money, although ultimately ruled in his favour.

title: Thrown Sisters
desc: A four-bedroom house became home to a prolonged poltergeist occurrence which threw two sisters from their beds and moved upstairs furniture when the family were all downstairs. On one occasion, the eldest sister was locked in the bathroom and engulfed by the shower curtain. Animals refused to go to the upper part of the building.

title: Young Boy
desc: A photograph taken by the family here showed a smiling young lad, around fourteen years of age, standing behind the sofa. On a different occasion, the father of the family asked the phantom to make him a cup of tea, after mistaking the entity as one of his sons.

title: George?
loc: Liverpool (Merseyside) - Private residence, Breeze Hill, Walton
desc: A former slave named George may have been responsible for this haunting, during which one man was slapped in the face as he lay in bed. Another person who rented the property left in tears, claiming he had been chased out by some form of angry spirit.

title: Ticking
loc: Liverpool (Merseyside) - Private residence, Calgarth Road, Huyton
desc: A couple left their home after a ticking started in their home. Clocks were stopped and removed, yet the sound continued and would move around the property, sometimes coming from the walls. An exorcism did not help, and after the ceremony, a coffee table was found upturned and pictures removed from the walls.

title: Moving Ornaments
desc: A family moved out of their property after enduring many strange events, including lights which switched themselves on and off, doors that opened unaided, and ornaments that moved by an unseen hand. A local press story claimed a vicar and housing officials also witnessed paranormal activity.

title: Thrower
desc: It was claimed that a poltergeist which started throwing items around in this property was witnessed by both occupants and police.

title: Encyclopaedia Moving
loc: Liverpool (Merseyside) - Private residence, Hale Road, Speke
desc: An outbreak of poltergeist tricks occurred in this property, including a set of twenty encyclopaedias moving from a chest of drawers to a table, a toilet flushing itself and bangs and knocks. Shadows of people would also appear on the walls of the living room.

title: Rapping
loc: Liverpool (Merseyside) - Private residence, Halewood Road, Gateacre
desc: The entity in this home could be heard rapping and occasionally tossed items around. The activity ceased after one occupant shouted 'go to hell' after small objects were thrown at him.

title: Floating Shadow
desc: A mother of two awoke in the early hours of the morning to see a shadow glide past her bed and move towards her daughter's room. As it moved, the entity turned its head to the woman, as if watching her. It vanished through the wall to the child's room. The woman was convinced that the shadow was a message that one of her children would die, and within a week, her daughter passed away.

title: Smoker
desc: Lights would turn themselves on and the smell of tobacco would fill the air. One visitor to the site reported seeing a black figure pass a bedroom door. The haunting was blamed on a former chain-smoking occupant who had died prior to the new owners moving in.

title: Tall Woman
desc: Despite living in their home undisturbed for 32 years, the Morgan family moved away after experiencing a poltergeist outbreak which tapped on their bedside table, flicked lights on and off, and held both occupants down on their bed. On one occasion, Mr Morgan watched a tall ghostly woman wearing a poke bonnet manifest; Mr Morgan fled the room. Although the family moved to Runcorn, the entity followed them.

title: Pushing
loc: Liverpool (Merseyside) - Private residence, Old Swan area
desc: A property here was said to contain something that would try to push occupants down the stairs and generate a bad smell.

title: Bouncing Ball
loc: Liverpool (Merseyside) - Private residence, Old Swan area
desc: Over a three year period, the five occupants of this detected house would hear a bouncing ball the source of which could never be discovered. The bouncing was originally heard coming from the attic but eventually spread to the entire house and would occasionally wake the occupants late at night.

title: Victorian Woman
loc: Liverpool (Merseyside) - Private residence, Old Swan area
desc: A witness staying at this property watched as a woman in Victorian clothing manifested close to him. The woman was grey and transparent, and moved in a weird, juddering way. The witness threw his bedcovers over his head in panic, waking his girlfriend who, after turning on the light, asked, 'you've seen her, haven't you?'. The witness only ever spotted the Victorian woman once.

title: Pusher
desc: A family left their home after a presence pushed a teenager, and a woman felt herself held down on a chair by an unseen force. Residents said they would feel something clinging to their clothing.

title: Water Water Everywhere
desc: This property has been subjected to dozens of water-related occurrences, including a leaking roof (although six roofers could not find a leak), water pouring through open windows, and an unexplained flood in the basement, where the water disappeared as quickly as it came.

title: Strange Man
loc: Liverpool (Merseyside) - Private residence, Woolfall area, Huyton
desc: Soon after a child in the house complained about the strange man standing by the toy box, various bumps and footsteps began to be heard in the house. A heavy chest of drawers tipped over, taking two people to lift it back into position. A local priest blessed the property.

title: Swishing
loc: Liverpool (Merseyside) - Private residences, Edge Hill area
desc: Footsteps which shook the bedroom were felt by two witnesses at different times, while a 'swishing' was heard as if someone were walking toward the kitchen and brushing the wall with clothing on several occasions. Large metal objects such as baking tins and colanders mysteriously disappeared and were never found. Another house on the same road reported poltergeist activity with heavy furniture being moved across the door in an empty bedroom, trousers flying around the room and people being awoken by loud clapping sounds.

title: Lady in Red
desc: One member of staff witnessed a ghostly older lady wearing a red cardigan in the bar area, while a few years earlier two stagehands watched a ghostly Cavalier emerge from a wall who turned to face the men before disappearing through the same wall. The site is also reputed to be haunted by a former caretaker.

title: Bride
desc: The old house which once stood here before the hospital was the scene of the ultimate wedding day disaster in which the bride fell to her death from an upper story window while her guests partied on below. Her shade has been reported by nurses in the newer building.

title: Liver Birds
desc: Several myths exist concerning the two metal birds perched on the Liver Building, all relating to the birds coming to life and departing the city, resulting in its downfall. One myth says the birds face away from each other to ensure they do not fall in love and become animated, while another story says if an honest man and a virgin woman meet and fall in love in front of the birds, the statues would spring into life.

title: Old Man
desc: Little is known about this shade that is sometimes seen drifting around the building.

title: Former Slaves
desc: Once held in cells on the site where the hospital was later constructed, many of the slaves still haunt this area.

title: Edinburgh
desc: A white city appeared for a short time over Liverpool - it was thought to be a mirage of Edinburgh, though no one could identify any of the buildings.

title: Mile Long Craft
desc: Lee Jones, his wife and her mother watched a huge saucer shaped craft hovering in the sky, clouds occasionally covering the object. A passenger jet that passed near the craft enabled Jones to estimate the ufo was about a mile long. Other witnesses reported seeing the craft throughout June and earlier in the year.

title: Cellar Dwellers
desc: Liverpool's oldest pub, the Slaughterhouse is reported to be haunted by a couple of shades who tend to enjoy lurking in the basement and making fleeting appearances in the bar.

title: Mary Norris
desc: Rather than face up to her husband's massive debts, Mary is said to have killed her son before taking her own life. Mary is said once to have manifested during a dinner party, most guests watching her disappear through a wall. Other people have reported the sounds of children crying during the night. A night fisherman at the pond heard a voice ask, 'have you caught anything yet?', but upon turning around, he could not see anyone nearby. Finally, two witnesses out walking after dusk in 2007 could hear the sound from a pack of hunting dogs emerging from dark woodland but were unable to spot the source. A modern myth appears to place a werewolf on the site.

title: Tablecloth
loc: Liverpool (Merseyside) - Springwood Avenue, close to Allerton Hall
desc: Two teenagers jogging along the avenue heard what they thought sounded like a horse a short distance behind. Turning to have a look, they observed what appeared to be a tablecloth and a horse's body without a head running along. Frightened, the pair ran faster and when they turned again, the entity had gone.

title: Green Globe
desc: At least one witness spotted a strange green globe within the cemetery. Ghosts reported in the area including a limping man in Victorian attire and a woman in black. One piece of local folklore says the water from a natural spring in the cemetery turns black if boiled (although the Liverpool Echo debunked the claim in 2017).

title: Cloudy Woman
loc: Liverpool (Merseyside) - The Grange Hotel, Aigburth (no longer operating)
desc: While staying at this hotel, one man twice spotted a cloudy shape in the form of a woman, although her features were hard to define. Both times the entity walked past the man and disappeared into a wall.

title: Funeral
desc: A witness was said to have watched a phantom funeral occur, complete with coffin and guests (with deathly pale faces). The witness was later told that many years previous, a secretive funeral had occurred along the road, setting off from a nearby hall at midnight.

title: Stroking
desc: Three generations of the Collins family and two lodgers fled this property the day after moving in. During their first night, one lodger heard footsteps and felt his bedsheets being removed from the bed, the eldest Collins felt a small, soft hand stroking their neck, while others heard running footsteps and felt 'something' follow them up the staircase.

title: A Five Shilling Encounter
loc: Liverpool (Merseyside) - Unknown house in Field Street
desc: Hugh Morgan was fined five shillings after being caught smashing a window of an empty house which was said to be haunted. Hugh claimed he was attempting to lay the ghost.

title: Footsteps
desc: A classroom in this school was locked up after staff and students heard heavy footsteps walking in the adjacent room but could find no one within. Dust on the floor was undisturbed. A local story said that a murder had been committed in the room many years previous. Before the building was taken over as a school, stories of ghosts were rumoured.

title: William Kennedy
loc: Liverpool (Merseyside) - Walton Gaol, prison cell G2
desc: Executed for murdering a policeman in the 1920s, Kennedy's shade remains in his former cell and continues to unnerve inmates.

title: Overwhelming Presence
desc: It is said that ever since the last steam engine left this site, an evil, repressive presence has descended upon the area.

title: Monk and Nun
desc: A local legend says that a monk and a nun were executed in the area after they were discovered having an affair. Another legend says that the children which the nuns had out of wedlock were buried along the lane. All are said to haunt their respective areas. A photograph taken in the area in 2012 was said to show a nun, monk and some of the children.

title: Monk
loc: Liverpool (Merseyside) - Walton, road close to St Mary's Church
desc: A bus driver on his way to work watched a monk cross the road in front of his car. The driver slowed and watched the monk vanish, initially believing the figure had gone down a subway. The driver later learned that the area was supposed to be haunted by a monk and nun.

title: Brother or Sister
loc: Liverpool (Merseyside) - Well in Everton area, but covered over pre 1859
desc: The site of a fratricide, the well was at one point considered haunted by the dead sibling before being covered over.

title: Young Man
desc: This phantom figure came and sat with one witness as he lay in bed, entering and leaving the room though a wall. The ghost's voice was said to be kind and gentle, and during life the man would come and play with the children here - the sighting occurred in a former children's playroom.

title: Rumoured
loc: Liverpool (Merseyside) - William Lockerby's home (no longer standing), Lockerby Road
desc: William Lockerby, after whom the street is named, owned a large house along the road, which had the reputation of being haunted (by who or what is not known).

title: Figure with Green Light
desc: Walking home late at night, a witness came across a shadowy figure holding an old fashioned lantern which glowed green. The figure walked quickly, crossed the road close to the cemetery and vanished into thin air.

title: Piping
desc: While phantom piping was mentioned in a 1976 newspaper article, no one seems to agree what, if anything, haunts the site.

title: Pale Figure
desc: This white figure in a long hanging garment (either a woman in a dress, or a monk or priest) haunts this area of town.

title: Hanging Highlanders
loc: Newton le Willows (Merseyside) - Hermitage Green Lane
desc: Caught by Cromwellian troops, these Highlanders were immediately hanged on the surrounding trees. The sound of running can be heard around the anniversary of the executions. A couple of people here in January 1990 heard loud drumming which moved down the lane, though nothing could be seen.

title: Old Lady in a White Hat
loc: Newton le Willows (Merseyside) - Private residence, Fern Avenue
desc: A family living at this council house moved in with neighbours after encountering a ghostly older woman wearing a white hat. Bangs, taps, and sounds of breaking glass were also heard.

title: Bride
loc: Newton le Willows (Merseyside) - Willow Park (and other meres and woods in the area)
desc: This woman in white is said to be a bride murdered by her husband on their wedding night hundreds of years ago. She may have last been seen by a married couple who spotted a figure with folded arms standing amongst trees. Two years prior to this sighting, two women passing Castle Hill observed the phantom woman in white.

title: Modern Myth?
loc: Sefton (Merseyside) - Church and roads in the area
desc: First-hand accounts appear to be rare, but one story says a nurse and her taxi driver both spotted a werewolf in this area.

title: Green Lady
desc: At least four army cadets returning to their HQ observed a green lady wearing an old fashioned dress and cardigan. Although her legs could not be seen, it looked as if the figure floated while crossing the fields and heading towards the church.

title: Presence on the Stairs
loc: Sefton (Merseyside) - Private house along Arundel Avenue
desc: A witness here heard the front door being opened by key - when she investigated, she saw nothing, though felt an invisible presence pushed past her.

title: Little Boy
loc: Sefton (Merseyside) - Private residence, Ford Lane, Litherland
desc: One man twice spotted a phantom little boy in the living room, while other family members heard strange sounds or felt 'someone' watching them.

title: Karaoke Screaming
loc: Sefton (Merseyside) - Private residence, Park Lane area
desc: The poltergeist here would unlock doors, turn lights on and move furniture around. In one instance screaming lasting five minutes emerged from a karaoke machine which had been stored on top of a wardrobe untouched for over a year.

title: Floating Seaman
loc: Sefton (Merseyside) - Punch Bowl Inn and nearby churchyard
desc: Thought to have drowned at sea and his body stored in the inn until burial, this blue clothed sailor has been observed floating around the building. Sometimes only his head and shoulders are visible, protruding from a misty base. The entity was also once seen nearby, appearing to be digging at a grave in the churchyard.

title: Chair of Despair
desc: A chair in this public house was reported as being cursed, after eight people who had used it died.

title: Face at the Window
loc: Southport (Merseyside) - Private residence near Meols Cop Station
desc: Lights would turn on and off, small items would be moved or thrown at occupants, and footsteps heard coming down the staircase. A shadowy figure would occasionally be spotted, and the face of an older person appeared at a bedroom window. The activity ceased after a blessing.

title: Woman
loc: Southport (Merseyside) - Sands Public House (no longer operating)
desc: A local story says a female phantom haunted this public house and would try to push people down the main staircase.

title: Former Occupants?
desc: There are many spooky stories told by past and present staff; the empty lift moves between floors at night, many reports of phantom figures exist, and sounds of footsteps are heard along deserted corridors. The bells for the call system have also gone off in empty rooms.

title: Tiny Alien
desc: A local woman took several photographs to test the camera on her new phone. The photographer later realised one of the images showed a tiny, 'grey' alien-like figure apparently walking along the road.

title: Rain of Stones
loc: St Helens (Merseyside) - Beecham's Pill Manufactory (now part of St Helens College)
desc: A poltergeist-like outbreak of stones that would rain down on floor workers resulted in police being deployed to find the source. A newspaper later reported that one officer spotted a man acting suspiciously, and when challenged, showed the policeman a mechanism that would catapult stones into the air. However, Mr Beecham disagreed with the report and said the mystery had never really been solved.

title: White Figure
desc: This pale figure, thought to be connected to the archaeological dig in the same area, is said to have once pushed a motorcyclist from his bike. It is still seen, normally lurking behind trees.

title: Face at the Window
loc: St Helens (Merseyside) - Croppers Hill, Prescot Road
desc: A factory which once stood here was reportedly haunted by a figure that would stare longingly through the windows of the building. Though the building no longer stands, local children still scare each other by saying the area remains haunted.

title: Stone Throwing
desc: Stones were thrown around the factory with no source being discovered.

title: Landing UFO
loc: St Helens (Merseyside) - Field in Rainhill area
desc: Robert Bennett told the St Helens Star newspaper how he had worked with police and radio enthusiasts in chasing a strange craft across the St Helens sky. The pursuit ended after three police officers watched the ufo take off after landing in a field.

title: Stone Throwing
desc: Stones, bricks, and potatoes would be thrown along this street after the sun went down. A projectile knocked off a police constable's helmet and other people suffered near misses. Although the local press played up the supernatural aspect of the incidents, the police believed they were looking for 'someone in the flesh'.

title: Jack
desc: A phantom nicknamed Jack, who may have been a former soldier, was one of several entities said to haunt this barracks.

title: Nun
loc: St Helens (Merseyside) - North Road, building which was once a convent
desc: Children at the school would report a phantom woman dressed in black and white, who appeared to take up residence in the upper part of the building.

title: Throaty Hiss
loc: St Helens (Merseyside) - Private residence, Junction Lane
desc: A visitor to the property heard a breathy, throaty hiss at the base of their bed. A few seconds later the same noise repeated next to their ear. The visitor said out loud that they were not scared and the sound ceased.

title: Grey Lady
desc: Two girls walking a dog spotted a ghostly figure emerge from nearby bushes. The ghost took the form of a young girl with shoulder-length blonde hair, wearing nineteenth century dress.

title: Man Dressed in Black
desc: There are several people in the running who could be this ghost (including a former manager and a Second World War pilot), who wears a black suit and long coat.

title: Old Nick
loc: Alderley Edge (Cheshire) - Devil's Grave, Stormy Point
desc: Legend has it that if one runs around the cave known locally as 'Devil's Grave' widdershins three times, the Devil is raised! Another version says that running around it three times restores your virginity.

title: Resting King
desc: Another place in the UK where King Arthur lies in wait for when he is required once more.

title: Naked Wizard
loc: Alderley Edge (Cheshire) - Likely to be around the B5087, but exact location not known
desc: Several witnesses have reported seeing a short old man, with a long white beard, running around naked in this area. Apparently, the figure was once approached by a police officer, only to vanish into thin air.

title: George
loc: Alderley Park (Cheshire) - Churchill Tree public house
desc: The poltergeist who slams doors shut and breaks the occasional glass has been nicknamed George. Shouting has also been heard, although no source found. It is speculated that the entity is connected to the site being used as a hospital during the First World War.

title: Pipe Smoker
desc: An aged figure has been observed on the site, puffing away at the demon weed. Some members of the cast and crew from BBC's Peaky Blinders were reported in the press as hearing a ghostly dog which haunts the site, shot dead by a gamekeeper after killing its owner.

title: Staring Man
loc: Audlem (Cheshire) - Audlem Road leading to Corbrook Court
desc: This entity manifested twice to the same witness, exactly a year separating the sightings. While driving down the road, the witness spotted the strange looking figure on the roadside, who stared into the car as he drove past. The figure did not appear in the rear view mirror.

title: Veiled Lady
desc: A black-clad woman with a veil, spotted several times walking the roads in the village during the early hours of the morning, became a talking point. One newspaper speculated the woman was less of a ghost and more of a practical joker.

title: Thing
loc: Barnton (Cheshire) - Unnamed road in the area
desc: Little is known about this phantom. One witness, returning from market with her pony and cart, described it as a large white 'thing'.

title: White Woman
desc: A lady in white haunts this field, while the road nearby is home to a phantom dog.

title: Hooded Figure
desc: A hooded figure crossing the bridge was spotted by a witness as she closed the lock gate. The woman's husband, travelling under the bridge at the time, did not see anything, but felt immense sadness and experienced a tingling on his face at the same time.

title: Floating Picture
desc: A former occupant of the hall told author Alan Garner that she had once watched a picture float off the wall.

title: Machine Worker
desc: The mill is reputedly home to the ghost of a female worker who died in a machine accident.

title: Old Lady
loc: Bollington (Cheshire) - Private house along Grimshaw Lane
desc: A former occupier of this house witnessed the ghost of an old lady who would stand in the corner of the kitchen. A phantom man would move around the property at night, and banging could be heard - the taps always coming in threes.

title: Gipsy Woman
loc: Bollington (Cheshire) - Ye Olde No. 3 public house
desc: The ghostly woman once reported here was said to be on the run from the police, and she drowned in a flooded stream nearby. A little girl was seen by a former landlady, who said the entity was dressed in blue, wore a poke bonnet, and walked straight through a closed bedroom door.

title: Not a Jogger
loc: Bosley (Cheshire) - Macclesfield Canal, first bridge after top of Bosley lock flight on the permanent boat moorings
desc: A ten year old girl pointed out a figure running across a nearby field to her mother, saying the word 'jogger'. The mother looked and could see the person in black moving towards them, but as it approached, realised that the 'jogger' wore a monk's habit and no face under his hood. The figure stopped a short distance away, as if paused in mid-sprint, and when the woman turned to check her daughter was okay (she had run off back to the boat), the monk vanished.

title: Running Man
loc: Boughton Heath (Cheshire) - Roads in the area
desc: Darting out from the side of the road, this speedy figure crosses in front of oncoming cars, before vanishing on the other side.

title: Floating Trees
loc: Brereton (Cheshire) - Body of water known as Blackmere, close to Brereton Hall
date: Prior to a death in the Brereton family
desc: Before the death of a member of the family, tree trunks would be seen floating in the water. Occasionally the water would also turn red.

title: Horseman
desc: A ghostly man on horseback is said to cross the lane before vanishing.

title: Strange Hound
desc: A phantom dog has been spotted in an area near the school.

title: Black Lady
loc: Burton (near Neston) (Cheshire) - Marshland between Burton and Harp Inn in Neston
desc: The story of a phantom black lady with a black dog which would cross the marshland was possibly a story manufactured so smugglers could work uninterrupted.

title: Nun
desc: The phantom nun said to haunt this building walks near the area of a secret passage. Her portrait hangs in the Nun's Room.

title: Headless Airman
desc: An airman has been observed standing around with no head - it is thought that he was decapitated as he tried to bail prior to crash landing.

title: Smoky Figures
desc: A group of grey shadows have been seen heading towards the vault, while a grey lady walks the building's corridors. One member of the family reported seeing a severed arm floating outside a window, trying to enter.

title: Old Monk
desc: A witness reported driving past an old monk standing on the side of the road. The figure did not appear to have any feet. As the witness pulled the car over and climbed out, the monk disappeared.

title: Bangs
loc: Chester (Cheshire) - Barlow's public house, aka Ye Old Vaults, 28 Bridge Street (no longer operational)
desc: Blamed on a former landlord, the haunting here consisted mainly of banging sounds and loud groans.

title: Maid
desc: A phantom maid, who died of starvation after being locked in a room, is reported to haunt the staircase, and appears only to men. Mild poltergeist activity is also reported at the site, and strange screeching noises have been picked up on a telephone answering machine.

title: Henrietta
loc: Chester (Cheshire) - Blue Bell Inn (currently East Glory Restaurant)
desc: Henrietta waited for her Royalist lover to return from the Battle of Rowton Moor, but soon discovered he had been killed. She committed suicide in the cellar. Henrietta's phantom is said to emerge from the cellar and walk to an upstairs window to wait for her lover to return.

title: Face
loc: Chester (Cheshire) - Bombay Palace restaurant, Upper Northgate Street
desc: Co-owner of the restaurant Aaron Ali claimed to have photographed a strange face in the building after hearing banging on a door. However, the face on the photograph does look very similar to one on a ghost creating mobile phone app.

title: Grey Figure
loc: Chester (Cheshire) - Canal path past Griffiths Corn Mill
desc: Walking home on a clear night, Mr Roberts watched as a pale grey figure emerged from the canal. The figure constantly changed shape and approached Roberts, who found himself frozen with fear. The figure surrounded the man, covering him in a clammy vapour, breaking Roberts from his paralysis and enabling him to run screaming from the site.

title: Dry Man
desc: Walking home soaked after a paper round, a teenage boy spotted a blonde haired man wearing a white shirt, grey trousers and black boots standing by a gate leading to a cycle path. The teenager passed the man, and turned to have another look at his boots, only to find the figure had vanished. After the event, the paperboy realised that the man was completely dry, despite the heavy rain.

title: Silky
desc: A former mistress of a Duke of Argyll, this white woman has yet to leave the bedroom of this house.

title: Sliding Ashtrays
loc: Chester (Cheshire) - Coach and Horses Public House, Northgate Street
desc: Regular drinkers at the pub have seen ashtrays move themselves across tabletops and strange blue light flash from the walls.

title: Footsteps
loc: Chester (Cheshire) - Daisy and Tom Toy Shop (no longer open), Watergate Street
desc: Former staff from this store reported footsteps, the smell of pipe tobacco, something which rattled the heavy fire door, and a stock room which was blocked by a heavy table from the inside.

title: Roman
loc: Chester (Cheshire) - George and Dragon public house, 1 Liverpool Road
desc: These phantom footfalls can be heard as they take a path that now leads through several partitioned walls - it is believed to be either a single Roman centurion on guard duty, or several soldiers who march from the front of the cellar to the back.

title: Romans
desc: It is reported that the pub was built on a former Roman camp, which is why twenty Roman soldiers and an officer have been seen marching through a wall in the cellar.

title: Sarah
loc: Chester (Cheshire) - House of Bewlay Tobacconist (would become Thorntons Chocolate shop), Eastgate Street
desc: Staff would be disturbed by the sound of footsteps and a woman sobbing. Poltergeist activity would also occur; doors opened, a picture fell to the floor, and decorative studwork forcefully removed.

title: Landlord
desc: The misspelling of the pub signage is said to be due to a nineteenth century sign writer encountering the ghost of a former landlord who slit his own throat; in the worker's haste to complete the job, the man failed to spot his typographical error. Since this time, the phantom landlord has been heard gurgling in the basement.

title: Moving Beds
date: Pre-1991 (noises) and man in brown in 1976
desc: A former member of staff at the site and a colleague heard beds being moved in the ward above them, then realised the floor above was closed and empty. Another time the worker and another person heard voices and footsteps emerging from another empty ward. A man dressed in a brown suit was seen visiting his mother in 1976, although this woman later said her son had died years earlier.

title: Jack
loc: Chester (Cheshire) - Old Fire Station Restaurant, Northdate Street
desc: Sporting a beard, this phantom fireman wearing a brass helmet was known only as Jack. A fireman who watched the figure sitting on a ladder was so shocked he rang the emergency bell to summon help. Even though the phantom had vanished by the time other people arrived on the scene, the witness quit his job soon after.

title: Man in Blue Overalls
loc: Chester (Cheshire) - Old lead steel works (no longer standing)
desc: This ghost, said to be a workman who died after being hit by a train, may never be seen again: the area he haunted was scheduled for demolition and new flats will be built on the former works site.

title: Meowing
loc: Chester (Cheshire) - Overpool Road, near Charter Crescent junction
desc: Malcolm Pennicard and his car featured in the news in July after reporting a ghostly meowing coming from his car whenever he drove along Overpool Road.

title: Herbert & Charlie
loc: Chester (Cheshire) - Pepper Street garage (no longer operational, was based next to what is now Habitat)
desc: These two phantom monks were spotted several times by staff working at the garage shortly after it began opening 24 hours a day.

title: Man in Cellar
desc: The man in the cellar of this pub is said to date from the seventeenth century, while the upper part of the building is haunted by a Victorian-era maid.

title: Moving Furniture
desc: Two visitors to this property heard unexplained noises, footsteps, and furniture being moved during their stay. A window would also open and close itself.

title: Lady
loc: Chester (Cheshire) - Private residence, Newry Park area
desc: Soon after moving into this property, a phantom woman walked past one occupant, and another witness experienced a cold spot which manifested by the side of a bed. A child who walked through one room returned a few moments later to find a chair had been turned upside down.

title: Plate Thrower
loc: Chester (Cheshire) - Private residence, south-west of city centre
desc: Occupants of this property reported plates which flew from cupboards, lights turning on and off unaided, and the sound of banging and running across the landing at night. A strange female figure glimpsed at the top of the staircase which they considered 'sad'.

title: Little Girl
desc: In an area thought to be a former nursery, people are said to have their hair pulled by a phantom female child.

title: Jenny
loc: Chester (Cheshire) - River Dee, area known as The Groves
desc: Jenny is said to wait just beneath the waters of the river, waiting for an unsuspecting man to grab and drown. A Viking warrior is also reputed to haunt the same area.

title: Legionnaire
desc: This trooper walks along the walls that once protected his garrison. One legend identifies him as an officer who fell in love with a Celtic girl; one fateful day he left his post to meet her, only to let Celtic warriors enter the city and cause chaos. Some have also reported a Cavalier in the same area.

title: Squeaking Cycle
loc: Chester (Cheshire) - Saltney Junction railway station, area of
date: Early winter mornings (recurring), last seen early/mid twentieth century?
desc: The phantom bicycle with a squeaking wheel was encountered by a guard and a child in the early hours of the morning, vanishing before it reached the witnesses. The haunting reputedly began after a suicide in a nearby work area.

title: Grey Monk
desc: Heard talking in old English, this figure traditionally walks around the cathedral and made several appearances during the 1970s. On Halloween in 2003 a group of children approached the monk thinking he was a man dressed up for the occasion. When a bag was held out at him and one of the children asked, 'trick or treat', he replied 'I'll have a treat' before sticking his head into the container and eating the contents (wrappers and all).

title: Elizabeth Warburton
desc: Several ghosts are said to reside at the building, including Elizabeth Warburton, a former owner who has been spotted walking through a wall, and a man in Tudor clothing. Other entities observed consist of a Second World War Officer and a grey haired woman sitting by the piano, while bangs, children crying, and disembodied footsteps have been heard.

title: Lady in a Bonnet
desc: Wearing a white nightgown and bonnet, this phantom was observed walking through a locked door. The witness questioned their sanity before being told that others had seen the entity.

title: Sighs of Criminals
loc: Chester (Cheshire) - The Bridge of Sighs, near Northgate
desc: A man cycling to an appointment along Northgate Street looked up at the bridge and spotted two or three people dressed in old fashioned clothing. They then vanished, leaving the man rather surprised. Prisoners being led to church prior to execution would cross this bridge, and it is believed their sighs can still be heard.

title: Royalist
desc: A headless Royalist soldier is said to haunt the building where he lost his head after a cannon ball hit him during his stay. The site is also reputed to be haunted by a grey lady.

title: Lioness
desc: A reported lioness was spotted roaming the area, though a police search could find nothing.

title: Woman in Black
loc: Chester (Cheshire) - West Cheshire Hospital campus, Liverpool Road
desc: The ghostly stories concerning the woman in black who is said to haunt this site are said to go back many years. On one occasion, a guard was said to have seen the figure sitting at a desk, but when he looked again, the entity had vanished. Footsteps have also been heard walking down empty corridors.

title: Fighting Men
loc: Chester (Cheshire) - Ye Olde King's Head public house
desc: Two men, who managed to kill each other while fighting over the love of a girl, are said to remain in the upper part of this pub.

title: Strange Voice
desc: A weird voice was picked up on a tape recorder during a ghost watch at this building.

title: Hanging Around
desc: Two felons hanged along this road are thought to have remained in the area.

title: Grey Figure
desc: A driver reported seeing a figure walking along the pavement, head down, illuminated by the lights on an oncoming car. The driver said the figure was completely grey - no other details could be seen. The figure dropped out of sight as the oncoming car passed, and when the driver reached the same spot along the road, the figure had vanished.

title: Uneasy Atmosphere
loc: Church Lawton (Cheshire) - Woodland near the lake
desc: Two friends were walking their dog in the woodland and encountered an increasingly uneasy atmosphere. They heard an iron entry gate screech open then slam shut and a series of footsteps walking towards them. The dog started uncontrollably barking at nothing which could be seen and then bolted straight towards the gate, the two witnesses following close behind. There is a local legend that the lake and surrounding area are haunted by a Grey Lady. She was somnambulant and ended up drowning in the lake during one of her sleepwalking episodes.

title: Woman in the Red Scarf
loc: Church Minshull (Cheshire) - Road to Winsford, near cemetery
desc: A figure of a woman in a red scarf whose pallid face was darkened only by black sunken eyes was seen by two people driving along this road. They reported that the ghostly figure stared right through them, was totally motionless and that her clothing looked like it dated from the 1960 or 1970s. When they drove past again the following day, the whole area seemed very different from previous.

title: Marbury Lady
loc: Comberbatch (Cheshire) - Marbury Park and former hall (no longer standing)
date: Exact date unknown, but reported to be around 22:30h (female ghost)
desc: An Egyptian maid was pushed down the staircase of the old manor house, dying in the fall. Her ghost was said to haunt the old hall, though when it was demolished, the spirit changed location and took up residence in the park. A phantom mare named Marbury Dunne is also said to haunt the park. The lady featured in the press in 1978 after a 'ghost' spotted by a driver transpired to be a dummy.

title: Lord in Chair
date: Ghost photographed in 1891, child appears prior to a death
desc: An early photograph taken here shows what appears to be a phantom man sitting in a chair in the study. Though the figure was identified as the late Lord Combermere, it is more likely a mortal blurred by a long exposure time. Another entity that takes the form of a small child is said to appear before a death in the Cotton family, while it was believed in the nineteenth century the site to be haunted by cowled monks.

title: Something Large
desc: Something tore a large hole in a pike net, and a diver searching for a drowned body encountered something that frightened him to such an extent that he said he would never return to the lake.

title: Bell Overboard
desc: After the nearby abbey fell into ruin, the bells were taken across the lake towards Wrenbury church - one bell fell overboard and can sometimes be heard ringing.

title: Piano
loc: Congleton (Cheshire) - Lion and Bell public house (was renamed Bar Twelve, as of 2011 closed)
desc: A piano was said to play itself, even though most of the keys were broken. The site was also said to be home to an old woman with her hair tied up in a bun.

title: Face in the Fireplace
desc: A thirteen year old girl reported seeing a face appear in the fireplace here which gave her 'disapproving' looks.

title: Crocodile
loc: Congleton (Cheshire) - Old quarry (now Astbury Mere Water Park)
desc: A lizard-like creature just under a metre in length was seen by several users of this quarry when it was converted to a water sports centre.

title: Raven
loc: Coppenhall (Cheshire) - Area around Don Kinson's Oak
desc: Thought by locals to contain the spirit of a woman who drowned herself in a nearby pool of water, this black bird had to be exorcised by the area's Bishop.

title: Grace Trigg
loc: Cotton Edmunds (Cheshire) - Cotton Farm, the 'Roman Bridges'
desc: Grace is said to have been beheaded by Cromwellian soldiers after trying to protect her master's property from theft and destruction. Some believe her spirit to remain in the area, carrying her severed head under one arm.

title: Grey Lady
desc: A ghostly grey lady is said to be seen (and heard) as she moves along a corridor in the hotel.

title: Ballet Dancer
desc: The stage door is reputedly haunted by an actor murdered by a jealous thespian. A ballet dancer who killed herself can sometimes be seen dancing on stage. She was last observed in a full white period dress and is said to leave a lingering smell of perfume.

title: Airman or Farmer
desc: This ghost, who appears all over the student's campus, is thought to be either a farmer or an airman who died on the site. Though seen on CCTV, the entity appears to have the ability not to show up on the video footage.

title: Robed Figure
desc: A photograph taken of the cellar at this public house is said to show a robed figure holding an unknown item across its chest.

title: Bright Headlights
desc: While driving back from Liverpool, a driver spotted a bright pair of headlights rapidly approaching from behind. Just as the driver thought he would be overtaken, the lights vanished. Believing that a car had crashed, the driver turned around and looked for it, but could find nothing.

title: Cyclist
desc: Killed in an accident in the 1920s, it was reported that the former rider sometimes appeared on foot, walking next to witnesses before fading away.

title: Vanishing Lady
desc: An owner noticed that this grey lady always disappeared by walking into the same area in the wall - when the zone was knocked through, a skeleton was discovered.

title: White Lady
loc: Delamere Forest (Cheshire) - Deep within the forest, between Frodsham and Delamere Forest rail station
desc: While walking to Frodsham from the Delamere Forest station, two people encountered a white lady. She stared at them for a couple of minutes before floating upwards into the trees.

title: Small Carriage
loc: Delamere Forest (Cheshire) - Road by the Station Cafe
desc: Returning from a late shift at work, this witness drove past a horse pulling a small, two wheeled carriage that was dimly lit by lanterns. The driver of the carriage remained motionless as the witness's car went by.

title: Blanche
date: Weather Dependent: Stormy nights. Last seen circa 2004?
desc: A mistress of Sir Piers Leigh who died 1422, Blanche pined away after hearing news about his death. Pier's funeral procession is now seen advancing towards the house, with Blanche wailing a short distance behind it. Another group of ghosts, this time children, have been seen playing on a bed in the Knight's Bedroom. Blanche may have last been seen by three people arrested for trespassing nearby, with their three descriptions of the ghostly figure given to the police marrying up perfectly.

title: Hole
loc: Disley (Cheshire) - Road between Disley & Whaley Bridge - area is marked by a memorial stone
desc: The site of a murder of William Wood in 1823, the hole left in the ground caused by the impact of his head as it hit the grass has remained evermore; the grass in it died, no other plants will grow on the spot, and all attempts to fill the hole have failed. Well, a marker stone recording the murder is at the site, but the hole is no longer present!

title: Perfume
loc: Disley (Cheshire) - Road running by railway line
desc: A couple out walking on Christmas Day encountered an overwhelming scent of old fashioned perfume which they could taste at the back of the throat. No other person had been seen for hours.

title: Possessed PC
desc: A 'typical' poltergeist case (with thrown items and rearranged furniture), the outstanding feature of this case was a personal computer, a BBC B Microcomputer, that several 'spirits' used for communication purposes - possibly a first.

title: Royalist
desc: While named after a phantom seen nearby, the inn is home to three other ghosts. A former landlady spotted a Royalist courtier, near the bat and another male figure in the cellar. A woman dressed in white has been seen by other owners and customers.

title: Headless Dorothy
desc: A story says that young Dorothy was accidentally decapitated by her father as he tried to save her from a group of drunken Roundheads. Her headless form is now reported to drift aimlessly around the village. The local pub is named after her sad tale.

title: Architect
desc: Depending on the story, this man was either pushed or slipped from the roof while working on the building - either way, he has been named as the ghost that now walks the corridors.

title: Blur
desc: A strange creamy-coloured figure was caught on film in this building.

title: Crying Children
desc: Two young princes were once thrown off this bridge into the river below by Roger Mortimer - their cries for help now heard on windy or stormy nights.

title: Griffin
desc: The village blacksmith killed a griffin that threatened the safety of this community.

title: Thumping
desc: Jean Marc Mariole and wife Charlotte made the Mail's headlines in February after revealing they had to spend nights in hotels to escape the entity haunting their flat. They reported that the bed sheets would lift and fall, doors would close, a shower curtain slid backwards and forwards, and Jean felt heavy breathing on the back of his neck.

title: Mother
desc: Charlotte, owner of the establishment, claimed in the national press that her salon was haunted by the spirit of her mum. The smell of her mother's favourite food, burnt buttered toast, would suddenly fill the shop. A shadowy figure was also picked up on CCTV.

title: Jim Barrow
desc: Jim was disliked while living, local emotion soon turning to hate once the man returned to the area after he died. The noisy spirit was finally exorcised by a team of preachers.

title: Woman in Summer Dress
desc: An older woman was spotted sitting on a bench at the top of this hill. The woman was in her fifties or sixties, and wore a light summer dress, even though the day was cold and the rain fell hard. The witness glanced away for a moment, and when she looked back, the woman had vanished. The witness checked the bench (which was soaking wet) and the only possible hiding place (a nearby tree), but when she failed to find the woman, she felt her skin crawl and fled the scene.

title: Jinny
desc: Jinny Chorlton was said to have returned after her death. It would appear that after her old home was demolished, she did not come back again.

title: Mary Frinton
loc: Gawsworth (Cheshire) - Area between Harrington Arms Inn and the Old Hall
desc: A member of Queen Elizabeth I's court, Mary was known for her promiscuous lifestyle, though she finally settled down and married locally. She now patrols the area near her former home.

title: Woman in Black
desc: The driver and two passengers of a vehicle could clearly see the solid apparition of a woman dressed in a black Victorian-style dress, including a bonnet type hat. The woman stood motionless on the roadside, near a metal gate, and the witnesses were confident the figure would have been caught on the front and rear cameras which continuously recorded in the vehicle. When reviewing the footage, the location had been recorded but the figure was not visible.

title: Maggoty Johnson
desc: Maggoty Wood takes its name from Samuel Johnson, England's last professional jester, who is buried in the wood. A legend says that he appears to anyone who walks around the grave twelve times.

title: Thin Woman
desc: Returning over the hills from a friend's house, a driver spotted a woman on the side of the road. She was thin, tall, and eerie. The driver was scared and drove on, only to see the same woman two hundred yards (180 metres) further down the road. The driver did not use the road again.

title: Bill
desc: A former landlord of the pub, Bill, is reputed to haunt the building.

title: John Middleton
desc: The grave of Middleton can be found here, a local hero who stood around 282 centimetres tall.

title: Photographed Banana
desc: Though the building itself is not haunted, one story says that a family dining here had a poltergeist following them around wherever they went, and it appeared in a photograph taken at this site (taking the form of a misty banana!).

title: Frightened Woman
desc: A woman who died of fright when Prince Charles visited Handforth Hall in 1745 was said to continue to remain here. A gamekeeper with a black dog also haunted the area but may have been laid by a parson.

title: Melting Cyclist
loc: Holmes Chapel (Cheshire) - Main road near Jodrell Bank
desc: Headmaster John Williams spotted a cyclist on the road ahead during a dark and stormy night. The cyclist, a young blonde-haired man wearing jeans and a sweater, seemed to laugh before melting away. Williams observed that, despite the heavy rain, the cyclist looked dry.

title: Brown Lady
loc: Holmes Chapel (Cheshire) - Olde Red Lion public house
desc: The ghost of this phantom woman haunted a once sealed room in the pub, though there have not been any reported sightings as of late.

title: Man in Tweeds
loc: Hoylake (Cheshire) - Royal Hotel, and golf course
desc: Observed while walking the corridors, this spook wears a cap and tweed jacket. It may be the same entity that has been seen on the golf course, wearing clothing that can be dated to the century.

title: Leopard Cat
desc: A farmer claimed he shot at a large golden cat that was on his land.

title: The Thing of Delamere
desc: Many locals reported a dog-like creature in the forest here, standing sixty centimetres tall. While the beast was described as having a tail like a fox, it looked more like an Alsatian dog.

title: Hooded Figure
loc: Kingsley (Cheshire) - Road towards Frodsham, near cemetery
desc: A hooded figure, without visible legs, by the edge of the road was spotted by a driver. The entity crossed the road in front of oncoming traffic, although no vehicles reacted, and the figure vanished as the driver reached the spot where it had first been seen.

title: White Rider
desc: A witness who returned home after night fishing at the mere reported seeing a ghostly woman riding a horse around the lake.

title: Annie Sarah Pollitt
desc: Knutford's first May Queen is thought to haunt this pub, with many of the staff reporting sightings of her white ghostly form in the lower rooms.

title: White HGV
desc: A driver was terrified as a glowing white lorry charged towards him travelling the wrong way down the M6. He pulled onto the hard shoulder and closed his eyes, feeling the HGV drive past - but looking into his rear view mirror immediately after, there was nothing there.

title: Edward Higgins
desc: A former robber and burglar, Higgins was caught, killed, and now haunts the hotel where he made his base of operations. A phantom coach has been seen and heard moving over cobbles outside the building.

title: Figure
loc: Knutsford (Cheshire) - Tatton Mile (road running next to Tatton Park)
desc: Driving with his full beams on, in 2009 this driver spotted the figure of a man standing in the road with his hand out, as if he wanted the car to stop. As the car drew closer, the figure vanished, causing the driver to swerve out of shock. Twelve years later, a couple in their car spotted a tall dark figure facing the road by the end of the wall. The figure looked curious enough for them to turn the car around to have another look, but no one could be found and there was no other traffic.

title: Noises
desc: Since featuring on the television programme 'Most Haunted', the hall has gained a reputation for being creaky and spooky.

title: Smiling Man
loc: Little Sutton (Cheshire) - Early twentieth century house (name withheld)
desc: A child watched as a smiling man with outstretched hands, wearing a pinstripe suit, emerged from the bedroom wardrobe. The child's screams alerted her mother who rushed to investigate but was unable to find the intruder. Years later, the child identified the ghost from an old photograph of the former owners - the man had died in the bedroom. The property was also considered unlucky, with the child falling ill and losing a leg, and their father losing the top of a thumb in an accident.

title: Pig
desc: This phantom pig was illuminated by burning candles upon its back.

title: Swaying Glasses
desc: Several tabloid newspapers reported Nigel Ramsay, manager of the inn, had experienced several spooky occurrences on site, including swaying glasses and a flying TV remote control.

title: Beryl
desc: Thoughtfully nicknamed by staff and visitors, this old lady was seen in the pub.

title: Small Man
desc: More likely to be a distant folk memory than a true ghost story, the attic of this building was said to be haunted by a little man. In truth, James Wilson (a very short man) lived in the attic in the early nineteenth century, most likely to escape mockery, and after his death, his desire for privacy lived on in the minds of his neighbours.

title: Richard and Friends
desc: Landlord Sean Hutchinson claimed in the local press that fourteen entities haunt this pub, including Richard, a little boy who plays hide and seek, a grey lady, and something which likes to scream.

title: Severed Arm
desc: This ethereal limb has been seen trying to open a window in the premises! An assemblage of shadows has also been seen, lurking near the family vault, while a female form dressed in grey drifts around the ground floor.

title: Wish Steps
loc: Macclesfield (Cheshire) - Church of St Michael and All Angels
desc: Local legend says that if you can run up the cobbled steps in one breath you will receive anything you wish for.

title: Female in Old Attire
loc: Macclesfield (Cheshire) - Gawsworth Hall and general area
desc: A female phantom is reported to drift around the courtyard of Gawsworth Hall, patrolling nearby lanes, and in the churchyard. Some have named her as Mary Fitton, a lady-in-waiting to Queen Elizabeth I.

title: White Woman
loc: Macclesfield (Cheshire) - Kendel Road (area known locally as the Birdy)
desc: This area is reputed to be haunted by a white woman with no feet.

title: White Figure
loc: Macclesfield (Cheshire) - Large, private house near churchyard
desc: A family moved out of their home after seeing a white figure with a grotesque face in one of the rooms - the two witnesses knocked a door from its hinges while trying to escape the entity.

title: Jester
desc: A figure has been reported dancing about the woods, their clothing adjourned with bells. The grave of the last 'real' jester in England is housed in this wooded area, and it is believed that the shade is he.

title: Caroline and Friends
desc: In 2002, a worker at the museum encountered several ghostly children on the site, one of which followed her home. The ghosts were described as non-threatening. The Shadow Seekers paranormal team were called in 2007 and claimed to have used dowsing rods to determine that the spirits of four children remained in the mill - Caroline, Sarah, Rebecca and John.

title: Something
desc: A few references exist of this site being haunted, but by what and who is pretty unclear.

title: White Dog
desc: Departing the station, this train driver reported seeing a white misty dog move quickly across the track from left to right. One side of the railway stands a six metre high wall, while on the other a 3.5 metre high mesh fence - nowhere where the dog could have come from or disappeared to.

title: George
desc: This pub spirit is heard walking around at night, opening and closing doors.

title: Headless King Charles
desc: The headless ghost of King Charles has been seen here, though he never visited the place. The nearby river Goyt is haunted by a wailing woman who once lived at the hall - her lover was drowned in the river, and she waits and cries near the spot.

title: Singer
loc: Middlewich (Cheshire) - Chadwick Fields (adult day care centre), Coronation Road
desc: This noisy member of the building sings, walks around the upper part of the floor, slams doors, and sometimes locks the bathroom door, just for fun.

title: Slain Dragon
desc: A local story tells of how Sir Thomas Venables shot and killed a dragon here by shooting an arrow into the eye, just as it picked up a small child to eat.

title: Sister Ida
desc: Sister Ida's shade was thought to come back to bring attention to the suspicious death of the abbess. An unnamed road leading to the abbey is haunted by a decapitated head that rolls on the floor - this belonged to a monk murdered while taking a message to the building.

title: Fire Protection
desc: This house has a salamander carved into the wall to protect it from fire. It appears to have worked; a large blaze in the community in 1583 levelled most of the town but failed to touch the protected home.

title: Former Owner
desc: A former owner of the hotel killed himself with a shotgun after discovering his wife was having an affair. His ghost was blamed for ringing bells in the kitchen after it had been closed for the night.

title: Knuckle Rapping
desc: The home of Ernest Haywood featured in the news after a phantom started to create several sounds, including footsteps on the staircase, knuckles rapping on the wall, and the loud bang of a heavy sack being dropped.

title: Grey Lady
desc: This phantom lady is reputed to walk the corridors of the hotel leaving the scent of flowers as she passes. Her portrait hangs in the drawing room. Another phantom is that of a young lad who cries over his missing dog (the grave of which is close to the walled garden).

title: Priest
desc: An unknown priest once arrived here and gave mass before mysteriously vanishing. It was later discovered that his description matched that of a former priest buried in the churchyard.

title: Black Hound
desc: To see this huge black dog is normally a sign of ill fortune.

title: Sir Gaulter and Lady Friend
desc: These two figures reportedly haunt the shoreline of the Mersea.

title: Nun
desc: A former nunnery, this hall now claims to be home to a ghostly nun.

title: Stephanie
loc: Northwich (Cheshire) - Primary School in the area
desc: A local myth tells of a young girl named Stephanie who died in a fire (or a car crash, or run over by a steamroller, depending on the story); her ghost returned to the school and could be heard screaming 'Mummy, mummy, nooo...!'

title: Jack
desc: A mother called in a clairvoyant after she heard a man's voice whispering over her baby's intercom. The house had been reported as haunted by its previous occupiers, by an old man named Jack who had died there.

title: Cavalier
desc: Several entities are said to be present at this venue, including a Cavalier and a child who ran through a wall.

title: Dropped by Old Nick
desc: The church once stood in the middle of the village, but the Devil tried to run off with it. He dropped the building where it currently stands when he heard the ringing of the bells at a nearby abbey.

title: Man in Bowler Hat
loc: Over Alderley (Cheshire) - School Lane, close to abandoned school
desc: After feeling uneasy and experiencing a sensation of being watched, a witness turned to find that she was being followed by a man wearing a bowler hat which cast a shadow over his face. The only sound the witness could hear was her own footsteps in the snow. Terrified, she fled.

title: Old Lady in Red
desc: This old woman often appeared wearing a large red cape, walking across one of the rooms before taking a seat and waiting for an unknown event.

title: Dueller and Wife
desc: The ghostly male figure was killed after a fight, his wife taking her own life in grief. Both figures stand together on the balcony.

title: Figure in Blue
desc: The only person waiting at the station watched as a figure in blue crossed the platform and down onto the tracks, where it appeared to lay and disappear from view. The witness walked to the platform edge and looked for the figure, but no one could be seen. The story was later told to another person, who said the figure had been seen previously.

title: Cattle Killer
loc: Preston Brook (Cheshire) - Headless cross (a sandstone block) in a field near Newton crossroads (may have been moved for the M56 construction)
desc: Two stones once stood here and were moved to a ditch by a farmer who wanted to clear the land. Soon after the removal, the farmer's cattle died, the spring water ran red, and the farmhouse became home to a violent poltergeist which smashed mirrors and windows. Normality returned when the stones were replaced.

title: Lychgate
desc: Newly married couples avoided passing through the Lychgate as it was believed the marriage would fail, either by discontent or death.

title: Mermaid
desc: Her motivation unknown, this mermaid returns once a year to sing and ring a bell hidden deep underwater.

title: Musket Fire
desc: Belonging to Civil War soldiers, the exchange of small arms fire still echoes around the area where a battle once raged. The sound of a crying child has also been reported at night.

title: Big Man
desc: A seven foot tall ghostly figure had been seen at the site. Poltergeist-like effects were also felt here, including many household items being found broken, banging, and tables violently shaking without anyone near. After ten weeks, the entity left the property and never returned.

title: Former Foreman
desc: A foreman who died two days after retiring in the 1960s manifested and knocked a pot of tea from the hands of a worker. Both the assaulted man and a witness were treated for shock. However, a spokesman for the plant said there was no evidence that the event had occurred and no record of any visits to the infirmary. Another story claimed that the number 14 boiler was also haunted.

title: Cattle Eaters
desc: Before the town was built here, legend says the area was home to a huge fire breathing dragon that was slain by a local blacksmith annoyed at the large number of cattle he and his friends were losing.

title: Choir
desc: A trespasser on the site claimed to hear beautiful singing while on the site, as well as seeing a couple of glowing monks.

title: Pigs
loc: Runcorn (Cheshire) - Pool Farm (demolished, replaced by Spur Road bridge)
desc: Fifty-three of Howard Crowther's pigs died over two weeks in August. While swine fever was initially suspected, forensic tests could not detect the disease. Around the same time, a black cloud, around ten-foot (three metres) high, began to be seen moving around the farm, on one occasion vanishing through the wall of the pig shed. The cloud was last seen in November, moving away from Howard as he approached it. As a side note, folklore said the farmhouse contained a secret passageway leading to Norton Priory.

title: Knocking
desc: After moving away from their home in Liverpool to escape a poltergeist, the Morgan family found themselves once again experiencing strange activity in the form of knocking on their bedhead and a 'presence'. A vicar began to regularly visit the property to help the couple, and although the activity died down in March 1972, it resumed after four weeks. The Morgans featured in the press five years later, reporting the entity continued to harass them, jabbing their ribs and hitting their heads.

title: Superhero
loc: Runcorn (Cheshire) - Town Park area and a location close to the Royal British Legion
desc: On two occasions witnesses claimed that a figure dressed all in black with red glowing eyes had prevented crime. In the first instance the figure had prevented a motorbike theft, and in the second had taken on a gang of six young people, disarming them before disappearing into the night.

title: Whispers
desc: Customers at this site would hear whispering close to their ear and footsteps walking across the ceiling. One story claimed that a farm once stood on the site; a mother locked her daughter in a barn for punishment. The barn burnt down, killing the daughter and driving her father mad with grief - he locked his wife in the farm's attic for a decade.

title: Levitating Egg
loc: Sandbach (Cheshire) - Caravan (no longer there), Fields Farm
desc: Reported in the local press, a caravan housing the Bebbington family also became home for a poltergeist who smashed windows and levitated an egg from the fridge.
