Even though the family believed the activity had calmed after an exorcism, they moved to a house three miles away. It was later claimed that the entity was Henry Scragg, born at the farm in 1840.

title: You
desc: The only thing known about this spooky entity is that it is named only 'You'.

title: Sir John Radcliffe
desc: A sixteenth century owner of the building, Sir John is said to be only one of fourteen entities which have been reported on site, including a lady dressed in a beekeeper's outfit.

title: Monk
loc: Sandbach (Cheshire) - Private house along Park Lane
desc: This phantom monk was said to have manifested to Christmas Carollers during the 1930s, and although not malevolent, continues to wake people who sleep in the house. The figure is said to wear shoes which curl upwards at the toe.

title: Scots
desc: A battle occurred here between Scots and locals in 1651 - the shades of the defeated Scottish troops are reported to be still at unrest.

title: Boots
desc: A large door would be heard closing itself, while others reported the sound of heavy boots coming from the empty hall. It was reported that locals believed the sounds to be created by the ghost of a sergeant who had died some time previous.

title: Traffic Deadlock
desc: Once a year, the Brereton family return from the grave to rendezvous at this church - their phantom coaches are reported to create tailbacks!

title: Moving Island
desc: A knight was convinced that his girlfriend was seeing another man and told her he would never see her again until the island in the lake moved - it promptly started drifting and has done so ever since.

title: Floating Bowl
desc: A former occupier of this property reported witnessing mild poltergeist-like effects while here, including a bowl floating in mid-air, the pulling of hair, and sounds of crashing plates in the kitchen.

title: Headless Kidnapper
desc: A member of the Spurstow family was beheaded when a kidnap attempt that he had masterminded went wrong. The headless phantom now walks along the appropriately named road.

title: Former Workers
desc: The National Trust named the mill in their top ten most haunted locations, claiming a gang of former workers were still residing there.

title: Old Man Marriott
loc: Sutton Lane End (Cheshire) - Rossendale wood (known locally as Marriott`s Wood)
date: Unknown, said to occur around midnight
desc: A ghostly figure of Old Man Marriott is said to walk down the road with his sheep dog and his gun.

title: Elizabeth
desc: A visitor sitting with their back to an alcove spotted something black behind them. Expecting to see someone standing there, the visitor turned around, but there was nothing there. A member of staff told the visitor that the site was once a nunnery and that the pub was haunted by a nun by the name of Elizabeth.

title: Cromwellian Victim
loc: Tarvin (Cheshire) - Bridle path near The Headless Woman inn, running from Hockenhull Hall
desc: An old servant woman was decapitated by agents of Cromwell, after she refused to hand over the location of her master's fortune. The woman's ghost made so many appearances that they named the nearby public house after the entity.

title: Aging Woman
desc: The artist Reginald Easton reported waking during the night and seeing an old woman standing by his bed when he spent a night at the hall. He was so impressed he spent a further week at the hall, drawing the ghost when he saw it. She is believed to have murdered a child in the hall.

title: Windy Man and Dog
loc: Tiverton (Cheshire) - Country lane between village and Chester
desc: Driving, lost, through the country lanes, a driver spotted a man wearing khaki walking a dog. Although the night was calm, the man and dog looked as if they were walking in a strong wind, with the dog's saliva blowing backwards. The driver pulled alongside the pair and asked for directions. The man did not answer, but glared at the driver, who could now hear a strong wind. Quickly leaving without an answer, the driver looked back but the man and the dog had vanished.

title: Old Woman
desc: The shade of an old woman is reported to sit under this group of trees.

title: Pet Duck
desc: This tame bird was killed by a landlord after it took to attacking patrons. Unfortunately, death failed to prevent the ankle pecker continuing its work, and it fell on members of the clergy to exorcise the spirit.

title: Trapped in a Bird
desc: A priest called in to deal with a troublesome spirit managed to trap the entity within the body of a blackbird. It is said that all the blackbirds on the grounds of the hall today are descended from that particular bird.

title: Mr McGraw
desc: Dressed in his headmaster's gown, this figure has been both seen and heard on different occasions - when seen by a cleaner, she convinced the caretaker to arm himself with a pistol and search the area!

title: Man with Slick White Hair
loc: Warrington (Cheshire) - A50 leading to Warrington from Knutford
desc: A driver speeding down the A50 passed a man in the road who tried to flag him down. The figure, with slicked back white hair, wore black clothing. The driver decided to go back and help the man, stopping about a kilometre further along the road, but to his horror realised the man was now standing a couple of metres behind his car - it would have been impossible for the figure to catch up with the vehicle in such a short period of time. The driver drove off again, not wanting to engage with the man with the white hair.

title: White Rabbit
loc: Warrington (Cheshire) - Bank Quay (possibly predating the railway station)
desc: Witnesses who spotted the phantom white rabbit would soon have a family member die.

title: Man and Young Boy
desc: Killed in an accident on the road outside, the pub is now home to an older man and a young boy. Staff have reportedly observed figures who disappear into empty rooms. Mild poltergeist activity, such as glasses being thrown off shelves, has also been observed.

title: Murder Victim
desc: His life snuffed out at some point in the 1930s, this shade has remained earthbound since. The hall may also be haunted by a white Lady, thought to be Lady Isabella le Botelor.

title: Giles
loc: Warrington (Cheshire) - Black Horse Inn (no longer operational), Liverpool Street
desc: One story says that the area around the inn is haunted by a stumbling and/or crawling figure who vanishes when approached. Some name him as Giles Boston, mortally injured during a fight with Royalist troops. The figure may have last been seen on the street outside the inn when a witness spotted an injured man crawling along the road; the figure vanished when the witness moved close.

title: Figure with Laser Eyes
loc: Warrington (Cheshire) - Drayton Road, Risley exit from the motorway, and Warrington Road
desc: A driver pulled over to watch a two metre tall creature, dressed in silver and with thin beams of light coming from its large eyes, as it moved along the embankment by the side of the road. When the witness arrived home, he discovered that he had 'lost' almost an hour. Just prior to the driver's sighting, a local woman spotted the figure from her garden as it walked through the former munitions factory on Warrington Road.

title: Grey Lady
loc: Warrington (Cheshire) - Hollins Park House (aka Winwick Hall, former hospital)
desc: This part of the old hospital site was said to be haunted by a grey lady and the sounds of children running and shouting. Other parts of the hospital, since demolished and replaced with a housing estate, were home to a phantom nun reputed to walk into one room here and take a seat before disappearing. She was said to be only visible from the knees up. Other phantoms included an American GI, white ladies, and former members of staff.

title: Stone Throwing
loc: Warrington (Cheshire) - Houses close to the churchyard, Stockton Heath
desc: Several greenhouses had glass broken after paving stones were dropped upon them. Despite sentries being posted, the source of the stones could not be found.

title: Dick Peabody
desc: This ghostly figure is blamed whenever a member of staff has their bottom pinched...

title: Banging
desc: Over a three-month period, knocking seemed to come from the ceilings and floors in the early hours of the morning, waking and upsetting the residents. After police and housing officials were unable to trace the source of the annoyance, residents requested a psychic researcher to rule out poltergeist activity.

title: Drinking Man
loc: Warrington (Cheshire) - Marquis of Granby public house
desc: A male figure moves through an area off-limits to customers and sits with a pint of beer before vanishing.

title: Tearaway Kids
loc: Warrington (Cheshire) - Marsh House Lane, private house
desc: A ghostbuster claimed to have rid this house of a total of five spirits, all teenagers or younger, who were making the homeowners life a living hell.

title: Military Man
desc: A signalman leaving his signal box after his shift in the sidings came face-to-face with a tall man in a military coat with large black buttons. The signalman closed his eyes in fright and when he opened them the man had vanished.

title: Heptagon
desc: From their back garden, a witness watched a dark grey heptagon shape silently fly over their house.

title: Small Figure
loc: Warrington (Cheshire) - Springfield Street Post Office (no longer operating)
desc: Waving out the window, this small figure could be seen from outside by a witness who later discovered the upper part of the building was empty and locked up.

title: Jenny Greenteeth
loc: Warrington (Cheshire) - Unknown pit in a field, Latchford
desc: Children were warned to stay away from a dangerous pit, as Jenny Greenteeth would drown them.

title: Banging Door
desc: A young married couple reported being woken by their bedroom door being thrown open by an invisible entity and slammed shut a few seconds later. They were later told an old woman haunted that particular bedroom.

title: White Ball
desc: A white ball of light bounced across the bonnet of a car before entering the vehicle. The driver experienced distorted vision and headaches for a few days following the incident.

title: Bakery
desc: Fortean TV reported this superstore as possessing ghosts in its EPOS room and bakery.

title: Human Fireball
desc: A girl walking down the stairs with a group of friends suddenly burst into flames. They quickly beat the flames out, but she later died of her injuries.

title: Banging
desc: Two brothers living in this house were subject to banging which emerged from the walls, loft, and doors. On one occasion, one resident was thrown out of bed after asking 'is that all the energy you have?' after feeling a small but constant vibration. The resident fled the room and told his brother of the event; the brother was overjoyed that he was not alone in experiencing the phenomenon.

title: Greenish Grey Craft
desc: While patrolling the town centre, PC Colin Perks spotted a hovering craft that glowed a greenish grey colour. Colin said the UFO was around thirty feet long and that he could see portholes along the side. After several seconds it flew off.

title: Anne Boleyn
loc: Wilmslow (Cheshire) - Bollin Hall (demolished nineteenth century, likely a railway viaduct now stands on the site)
desc: It was claimed that the hall was both the birthplace of Anne Boleyn and where her ghost returned.

title: Door Opener
loc: Wilmslow (Cheshire) - George and Dragon public house (no longer operating)
desc: As they were leaving, the publicans spoke to the press about their poltergeist, who opened doors, shook tables and moved pictures. One member of staff had fled the cellar after believing he had seen a ghost.

title: Young Woman in White
desc: This unnamed woman managed to accidentally lance an artery and bled to death in the 1770s. Her phantom was last encountered by an Irish labourer who spotted her surrounded by mist.

title: Man in Overcoat
desc: While cycling home, this witness spotted a man drifting along the road. The phantom wore a heavy long coat with a hat not too dissimilar to that which a cowboy would wear. The figure's legs were not visible. The witness watched the figure for around ten seconds and when eye contact was made, the apparition vanished.

title: Mirror Smasher
desc: An orb was blamed for smashing a mirror in the toilets when no one was present - footage of the incident was uploaded to YouTube.

title: Victorian Child
desc: Previous landlords were said to have encountered a Victorian child who wanders the corridors at night. The cellar is said to have a spooky atmosphere.

title: Pig the Builder
desc: The foundations of the church were set in another location, but a squealing pig moved them all in one night to the spot where St Oswald fell in battle. A carving of the pig exists in the church wall.

title: Hitchhiker in Leather
loc: Wybunbury (Cheshire) - A51 near to the town
desc: A driver picked up a male hitchhiker wearing old style motorbike leathers - a short while into the journey, the driver realised that the hitchhiker had vanished, though the seatbelt was still in place and the door locked.

title: Pacing
desc: It was reported in the local press during the 1970s that footsteps could be heard within this building coming from empty rooms, although a former worker at the site said that the story was a publicity stunt.

title: Old Woman
loc: Liverpool (Merseyside) - 82 Wimborne Road, Huyton (house no longer standing)
desc: A family living here were terrified by a phantom old lady who stood five-foot tall, bent over with a walking stick. Her face was little more than a shrivelled skull. Builders working close to the site quit once they heard an exorcism had taken place. The house has since been demolished.

title: Small Woman
loc: Liverpool (Merseyside) - 9 and 11 South Hunter Street (houses demolished in early 1960s)
desc: Seen by a mother and daughter on separate occasions, this phantom was described as a small woman wearing a lace cap and soft shawl. She was semi-transparent and vanished when approached.

title: George
desc: George has been seen several times standing by beds on the fifth floor.

title: Glowing Ball
desc: The hall is reputedly haunted by former residents and ghost hunts on the site have turned up flashes of light and sightings of glowing balls. An 'orb' caught on camera featured in the press in 2014.

title: The Sarge
loc: Liverpool (Merseyside) - Ambulance training centre, Quarry Street, Woolton
desc: For many years the building was reputedly haunted by an entity known as 'The Sarge' - a former policeman killed when the wheel of his patrol wagon struck a bollard and he was thrown to the ground. Ambulance crews reported phantom footsteps, breaking windows and doors which unlocked and opened themselves.

title: Flag Waver
loc: Liverpool (Merseyside) - Area around former Otterspool rail station
desc: Before closing in 1951, a teenager was saved by a man from being hit by a train, although the rescuer was killed in the process. He is said to wave a red warning flag in the area.

title: Smells and Shadows
loc: Liverpool (Merseyside) - Battle of the Atlantic Bunker
desc: A visitor to the site could smell perfume where a Wren had fallen to her death, spotted strange shadows, and experienced the sensation of being followed. When the witness returned years later, the location had changed and they experienced nothing untoward, although stories tell of figures in naval uniform who walk through walls.

title: Time Slip
desc: On various dates, several people (including an off duty policeman) have reported slipping back in time along this road, finding them surrounded by people dressed in clothing of the 1940s, with a cobbled street and old style shops.

title: Spookside
desc: It was reported in the local press that the cast of 'The Close', a low budget British horror film being filmed at the former soap opera site, regarded the set as haunted. Lights would flicker out at inopportune moments, items would disappear, and the final scene of the film was constantly cancelled as bad weather would come from nowhere.

title: George
loc: Liverpool (Merseyside) - Coach and Horses public house
desc: A former landlord, George still returns to keep a watchful eye on his former establishment.

title: Earl of Sefton
date: Late twentieth century, camera in April 2009, most recently July 2013
desc: The Sixth Earl of Sefton has been sighted walking through the tearoom and in his former bedroom. An incorporeal young boy was once seen standing by the fireplace in the dining room, while other strange shadows have been reported drifting down various corridors. Footage from a CCTV camera in April 2009 reputedly shows a phantom figure moving across the grounds, though the image is more likely to be a close-up of an insect. Two people exploring the basement in 2013 encountered a short hideous figure in a cloak, before later spotting the figure on the staircase where he vanished.

title: Gin Runner
loc: Liverpool (Merseyside) - David Lewis Northern Hospital (closed 1978 and demolished)
desc: Beaten to death nearby by Customs officers who caught the man trying to bring his illicit goods ashore, the ghost of the smuggler was reported in the hospital that was built close to the site of his murder. The site also had the reputation as being haunted by Nurse Jones, murdered at the site in 1919.

title: Spring Healed Jack
desc: This area was one from which this enigmatic creature/entity was reported.

title: Murdered Woman
loc: Liverpool (Merseyside) - Former hotel along Sir Thomas Street
desc: A voice in an empty toilet was heard issuing warnings of future events, while a figure was seen passing a door and climbing the stairs when the three people in the building were accounted for. A local legend says that a woman was murdered on the staircase close to the toilets.

title: Footsteps
loc: Liverpool (Merseyside) - Former police and fire station, Lark Lane
desc: Footsteps have been reported on the rear staircase and a heavy door opens and closes unaided, according to the Night Vision Investigations team.

title: Older Woman
loc: Liverpool (Merseyside) - Former post office (currently a computer centre)
desc: A woman in a checked red coat walked by two witnesses who were standing by a telephone box. The woman passed within thirty centimetres of the pair and proceeded to walk through the locked door to the post office.

title: Flying Glasses
loc: Liverpool (Merseyside) - Head of Steam public house, Lime Street
desc: Glasses are said to be thrown from shelves and people feel something following them upstairs.

title: Baby Bouncer
loc: Liverpool (Merseyside) - House owned by Liverpool Housing Trust, Madryn Street, Toxteth
desc: A family living here with a poltergeist reported that the entity picked up their young son and threw him from his cot. The entity would also move the washing machine around the kitchen, hide money, and smash ashtrays.

title: Purple Faced Girl
loc: Liverpool (Merseyside) - Huyton, streets in the area
desc: One local myth says certain streets were home to a blue/purple faced young girl who would follow families with children.

title: Lady in Blue
loc: Liverpool (Merseyside) - Jessie Appleton's public house (aka The Dingle) (no longer operating), Park Road
desc: Vicky Lee appeared in the press claiming her pub was haunted, having experienced footsteps in locked areas and unexplained breezes across the neck. Vicky's son encountered an older woman wearing a blue dress who vanished from a room.

title: Monk
loc: Liverpool (Merseyside) - Knowsley Hall and Riding Hill
desc: A phantom monk is said to haunt the area around the hall and the hill. A local legend says a secret tunnel ran from the monastery that once stood on the hill, and that the path the ghostly monk takes indicates the route of the passage.

title: Swinging Swain
loc: Liverpool (Merseyside) - Lea Hall (or possibly Lee Hall) (no longer standing), Gateacre
desc: A local villager who tried his luck with the squire's daughter found himself lynched from a tree close to the hall. On windy nights, the body could be heard swinging. A murder in the hall itself could be repeatedly heard, the moans of a woman and the laughter of her homicidal husband. A journalist who visited the hall between the world wars looking for ghosts to write about found himself frozen to the spot, surrounded by complete silence; he managed to escape and flee after hearing a clock striking in the distance.

title: Floating Torso
desc: Sightings of the ghost of Lime Street are said to go back hundreds or years. One of the more recent witnesses described the entity as being quite tall, though the legs could not be seen, with the mouth silently moving. An unnamed hotel (that later became offices) along the road is also haunted by the figure of a tall woman.

title: Thomas Campbell Black
loc: Liverpool (Merseyside) - Liverpool Airport, formerly known as Speke
desc: Black died in an accident on the runway of the airfield in 1936 - his shadowy form has been seen walking around the area where the old hangars stood.

title: Hitchhiker
desc: Killed in the middle of the twentieth century in the tunnel under the Mersey, this phantom hitchhiker is still occasionally seen.

title: The Demons Below See
desc: This old well has the words 'Qui non dat quod habet, Daemon infra vide 1414' carved above it. It was said that any traveller passing by would have no choice but to drink the waters and give a donation to charity, otherwise the Devil (chained under the well) would laugh.

title: Coal Thrower
loc: Liverpool (Merseyside) - Myers Street, Smithdown Lane (no longer exists)
desc: Many of the windows along this street were broken by thrown pieces of coal. The breakages continued after police began patrolling the area.

title: Voices
desc: A team of French film makers reportedly encountered children's voices, and a strange white mist while at this site. The former hospital grounds has a reputation for being haunted by a small child on the top floor, while dragging sounds have been reported elsewhere and small items associated with childhood thrown around.

title: Screeching Ginny
loc: Liverpool (Merseyside) - Old Garston Dock Station, and St Mary's Road, Garston
desc: The local witch known as Screeching Ginny appeared and gave chase to a group of school children who were playing on the disused tracks of the railway station. Folklore says the witch fell in love with a local boy but it was unrequited; as the boy left the area with his girlfriend on a train, Ginny threw herself on the tracks and died. Although the station is long gone, the witch still haunts the area.

title: Cloaked Figure
desc: A firefighter tackling a blaze in the former rectory believed he spotted a figure standing by the engine, although no one was there at the time. The building had a reputation as being haunted by the ghost of a cloaked figure.

title: Screaming Woman
desc: Two students sought help from a medium after enduring a phantom woman in her fifties who would scream during the night and call out the name 'Shelley Jones'. On one occasion the students returned to find the message 'get out' written out on the floor using their socks.

title: Upstairs Bangs
loc: Liverpool (Merseyside) - Private house along Sackville Street
desc: The upper part of the building was subjected to multiple bangs and crashes with no apparent source - the entity was also blamed for pushing a woman down the stairs, causing injuries that required hospital treatment.

title: Man
loc: Liverpool (Merseyside) - Private residence (likely no longer standing)
desc: An occupant observed a ghostly man standing on the scullery floor, the sight unnerving the witness to such an extent that the area was avoided. The floor would later collapse, revealing a hidden well where the figure had stood.

title: Murdered Man?
loc: Liverpool (Merseyside) - Private residence (likely no longer standing), Toxteth Park
desc: A court case revolved around a maid suing her employer for a month's salary having left her job after encountering a ghost. The maid stated the ghost had not unduly worried her, but stories about bodies being buried under the building had done so. The judge suggested that her former employer pay the outstanding money, although ultimately ruled in his favour.

title: Thrown Sisters
desc: A four-bedroom house became home to a prolonged poltergeist occurrence which threw two sisters from their beds and moved upstairs furniture when the family were all downstairs. On one occasion, the eldest sister was locked in the bathroom and engulfed by the shower curtain. Animals refused to go to the upper part of the building.

title: Young Boy
desc: A photograph taken by the family here showed a smiling young lad, around fourteen years of age, standing behind the sofa. On a different occasion, the father of the family asked the phantom to make him a cup of tea, after mistaking the entity as one of his sons.

title: George?
loc: Liverpool (Merseyside) - Private residence, Breeze Hill, Walton
desc: A former slave named George may have been responsible for this haunting, during which one man was slapped in the face as he lay in bed. Another person who rented the property left in tears, claiming he had been chased out by some form of angry spirit.

title: Ticking
loc: Liverpool (Merseyside) - Private residence, Calgarth Road, Huyton
desc: A couple left their home after a ticking started in their home. Clocks were stopped and removed, yet the sound continued and would move around the property, sometimes coming from the walls. An exorcism did not help, and after the ceremony, a coffee table was found upturned and pictures removed from the walls.

title: Moving Ornaments
desc: A family moved out of their property after enduring many strange events, including lights which switched themselves on and off, doors that opened unaided, and ornaments that moved by an unseen hand. A local press story claimed a vicar and housing officials also witnessed paranormal activity.

title: Thrower
desc: It was claimed that a poltergeist which started throwing items around in this property was witnessed by both occupants and police.

title: Encyclopaedia Moving
loc: Liverpool (Merseyside) - Private residence, Hale Road, Speke
desc: An outbreak of poltergeist tricks occurred in this property, including a set of twenty encyclopaedias moving from a chest of drawers to a table, a toilet flushing itself and bangs and knocks. Shadows of people would also appear on the walls of the living room.

title: Rapping
loc: Liverpool (Merseyside) - Private residence, Halewood Road, Gateacre
desc: The entity in this home could be heard rapping and occasionally tossed items around. The activity ceased after one occupant shouted 'go to hell' after small objects were thrown at him.

title: Floating Shadow
desc: A mother of two awoke in the early hours of the morning to see a shadow glide past her bed and move towards her daughter's room. As it moved, the entity turned its head to the woman, as if watching her. It vanished through the wall to the child's room. The woman was convinced that the shadow was a message that one of her children would die, and within a week, her daughter passed away.

title: Smoker
desc: Lights would turn themselves on and the smell of tobacco would fill the air. One visitor to the site reported seeing a black figure pass a bedroom door. The haunting was blamed on a former chain-smoking occupant who had died prior to the new owners moving in.

title: Tall Woman
desc: Despite living in their home undisturbed for 32 years, the Morgan family moved away after experiencing a poltergeist outbreak which tapped on their bedside table, flicked lights on and off, and held both occupants down on their bed. On one occasion, Mr Morgan watched a tall ghostly woman wearing a poke bonnet manifest; Mr Morgan fled the room. Although the family moved to Runcorn, the entity followed them.

title: Pushing
loc: Liverpool (Merseyside) - Private residence, Old Swan area
desc: A property here was said to contain something that would try to push occupants down the stairs and generate a bad smell.

title: Bouncing Ball
loc: Liverpool (Merseyside) - Private residence, Old Swan area
desc: Over a three year period, the five occupants of this detected house would hear a bouncing ball the source of which could never be discovered. The bouncing was originally heard coming from the attic but eventually spread to the entire house and would occasionally wake the occupants late at night.

title: Victorian Woman
loc: Liverpool (Merseyside) - Private residence, Old Swan area
desc: A witness staying at this property watched as a woman in Victorian clothing manifested close to him. The woman was grey and transparent, and moved in a weird, juddering way. The witness threw his bedcovers over his head in panic, waking his girlfriend who, after turning on the light, asked, 'you've seen her, haven't you?'. The witness only ever spotted the Victorian woman once.

title: Pusher
desc: A family left their home after a presence pushed a teenager, and a woman felt herself held down on a chair by an unseen force. Residents said they would feel something clinging to their clothing.

title: Water Water Everywhere
desc: This property has been subjected to dozens of water-related occurrences, including a leaking roof (although six roofers could not find a leak), water pouring through open windows, and an unexplained flood in the basement, where the water disappeared as quickly as it came.

title: Strange Man
loc: Liverpool (Merseyside) - Private residence, Woolfall area, Huyton
desc: Soon after a child in the house complained about the strange man standing by the toy box, various bumps and footsteps began to be heard in the house. A heavy chest of drawers tipped over, taking two people to lift it back into position. A local priest blessed the property.

title: Swishing
loc: Liverpool (Merseyside) - Private residences, Edge Hill area
desc: Footsteps which shook the bedroom were felt by two witnesses at different times, while a 'swishing' was heard as if someone were walking toward the kitchen and brushing the wall with clothing on several occasions. Large metal objects such as baking tins and colanders mysteriously disappeared and were never found. Another house on the same road reported poltergeist activity with heavy furniture being moved across the door in an empty bedroom, trousers flying around the room and people being awoken by loud clapping sounds.

title: Lady in Red
desc: One member of staff witnessed a ghostly older lady wearing a red cardigan in the bar area, while a few years earlier two stagehands watched a ghostly Cavalier emerge from a wall who turned to face the men before disappearing through the same wall. The site is also reputed to be haunted by a former caretaker.

title: Bride
desc: The old house which once stood here before the hospital was the scene of the ultimate wedding day disaster in which the bride fell to her death from an upper story window while her guests partied on below. Her shade has been reported by nurses in the newer building.

title: Liver Birds
desc: Several myths exist concerning the two metal birds perched on the Liver Building, all relating to the birds coming to life and departing the city, resulting in its downfall. One myth says the birds face away from each other to ensure they do not fall in love and become animated, while another story says if an honest man and a virgin woman meet and fall in love in front of the birds, the statues would spring into life.

title: Old Man
desc: Little is known about this shade that is sometimes seen drifting around the building.

title: Former Slaves
desc: Once held in cells on the site where the hospital was later constructed, many of the slaves still haunt this area.

title: Edinburgh
desc: A white city appeared for a short time over Liverpool - it was thought to be a mirage of Edinburgh, though no one could identify any of the buildings.

title: Mile Long Craft
desc: Lee Jones, his wife and her mother watched a huge saucer shaped craft hovering in the sky, clouds occasionally covering the object. A passenger jet that passed near the craft enabled Jones to estimate the ufo was about a mile long. Other witnesses reported seeing the craft throughout June and earlier in the year.

title: Cellar Dwellers
desc: Liverpool's oldest pub, the Slaughterhouse is reported to be haunted by a couple of shades who tend to enjoy lurking in the basement and making fleeting appearances in the bar.

title: Mary Norris
desc: Rather than face up to her husband's massive debts, Mary is said to have killed her son before taking her own life. Mary is said once to have manifested during a dinner party, most guests watching her disappear through a wall. Other people have reported the sounds of children crying during the night. A night fisherman at the pond heard a voice ask, 'have you caught anything yet?', but upon turning around, he could not see anyone nearby. Finally, two witnesses out walking after dusk in 2007 could hear the sound from a pack of hunting dogs emerging from dark woodland but were unable to spot the source. A modern myth appears to place a werewolf on the site.

title: Tablecloth
loc: Liverpool (Merseyside) - Springwood Avenue, close to Allerton Hall
desc: Two teenagers jogging along the avenue heard what they thought sounded like a horse a short distance behind. Turning to have a look, they observed what appeared to be a tablecloth and a horse's body without a head running along. Frightened, the pair ran faster and when they turned again, the entity had gone.

title: Green Globe
desc: At least one witness spotted a strange green globe within the cemetery. Ghosts reported in the area including a limping man in Victorian attire and a woman in black. One piece of local folklore says the water from a natural spring in the cemetery turns black if boiled (although the Liverpool Echo debunked the claim in 2017).

title: Cloudy Woman
loc: Liverpool (Merseyside) - The Grange Hotel, Aigburth (no longer operating)
desc: While staying at this hotel, one man twice spotted a cloudy shape in the form of a woman, although her features were hard to define. Both times the entity walked past the man and disappeared into a wall.

title: Funeral
desc: A witness was said to have watched a phantom funeral occur, complete with coffin and guests (with deathly pale faces). The witness was later told that many years previous, a secretive funeral had occurred along the road, setting off from a nearby hall at midnight.

title: Stroking
desc: Three generations of the Collins family and two lodgers fled this property the day after moving in. During their first night, one lodger heard footsteps and felt his bedsheets being removed from the bed, the eldest Collins felt a small, soft hand stroking their neck, while others heard running footsteps and felt 'something' follow them up the staircase.

title: A Five Shilling Encounter
loc: Liverpool (Merseyside) - Unknown house in Field Street
desc: Hugh Morgan was fined five shillings after being caught smashing a window of an empty house which was said to be haunted. Hugh claimed he was attempting to lay the ghost.

title: Footsteps
desc: A classroom in this school was locked up after staff and students heard heavy footsteps walking in the adjacent room but could find no one within. Dust on the floor was undisturbed. A local story said that a murder had been committed in the room many years previous. Before the building was taken over as a school, stories of ghosts were rumoured.

title: William Kennedy
loc: Liverpool (Merseyside) - Walton Gaol, prison cell G2
desc: Executed for murdering a policeman in the 1920s, Kennedy's shade remains in his former cell and continues to unnerve inmates.

title: Overwhelming Presence
desc: It is said that ever since the last steam engine left this site, an evil, repressive presence has descended upon the area.

title: Monk and Nun
desc: A local legend says that a monk and a nun were executed in the area after they were discovered having an affair. Another legend says that the children which the nuns had out of wedlock were buried along the lane. All are said to haunt their respective areas. A photograph taken in the area in 2012 was said to show a nun, monk and some of the children.

title: Monk
loc: Liverpool (Merseyside) - Walton, road close to St Mary's Church
desc: A bus driver on his way to work watched a monk cross the road in front of his car. The driver slowed and watched the monk vanish, initially believing the figure had gone down a subway. The driver later learned that the area was supposed to be haunted by a monk and nun.

title: Brother or Sister
loc: Liverpool (Merseyside) - Well in Everton area, but covered over pre 1859
desc: The site of a fratricide, the well was at one point considered haunted by the dead sibling before being covered over.

title: Young Man
desc: This phantom figure came and sat with one witness as he lay in bed, entering and leaving the room though a wall. The ghost's voice was said to be kind and gentle, and during life the man would come and play with the children here - the sighting occurred in a former children's playroom.

title: Rumoured
loc: Liverpool (Merseyside) - William Lockerby's home (no longer standing), Lockerby Road
desc: William Lockerby, after whom the street is named, owned a large house along the road, which had the reputation of being haunted (by who or what is not known).

title: Figure with Green Light
desc: Walking home late at night, a witness came across a shadowy figure holding an old fashioned lantern which glowed green. The figure walked quickly, crossed the road close to the cemetery and vanished into thin air.

title: Rumoured
loc: Liverpool (Merseyside) - William Lockerby's home (no longer standing), Lockerby Road
desc: William Lockerby, after whom the street is named, owned a large house along the road, which had the reputation of being haunted (by who or what is not known).

desc: Walking home late at night, a witness came across a shadowy figure holding an old fashioned lantern which glowed green. The figure walked quickly, crossed the road close to the cemetery and vanished into thin air.

title: Bangs
loc: Chester (Cheshire) - Barlow's public house, aka Ye Old Vaults, 28 Bridge Street (no longer operational)
desc: Blamed on a former landlord, the haunting here consisted mainly of banging sounds and loud groans.

title: Maid
desc: A phantom maid, who died of starvation after being locked in a room, is reported to haunt the staircase, and appears only to men. Mild poltergeist activity is also reported at the site, and strange screeching noises have been picked up on a telephone answering machine.

title: Henrietta
loc: Chester (Cheshire) - Blue Bell Inn (currently East Glory Restaurant)
desc: Henrietta waited for her Royalist lover to return from the Battle of Rowton Moor, but soon discovered he had been killed. She committed suicide in the cellar. Henrietta's phantom is said to emerge from the cellar and walk to an upstairs window to wait for her lover to return.

title: Face
loc: Chester (Cheshire) - Bombay Palace restaurant, Upper Northgate Street
desc: Co-owner of the restaurant Aaron Ali claimed to have photographed a strange face in the building after hearing banging on a door. However, the face on the photograph does look very similar to one on a ghost creating mobile phone app.

title: Grey Figure
loc: Chester (Cheshire) - Canal path past Griffiths Corn Mill
desc: Walking home on a clear night, Mr Roberts watched as a pale grey figure emerged from the canal. The figure constantly changed shape and approached Roberts, who found himself frozen with fear. The figure surrounded the man, covering him in a clammy vapour, breaking Roberts from his paralysis and enabling him to run screaming from the site.

title: Dry Man
desc: Walking home soaked after a paper round, a teenage boy spotted a blonde haired man wearing a white shirt, grey trousers and black boots standing by a gate leading to a cycle path. The teenager passed the man, and turned to have another look at his boots, only to find the figure had vanished. After the event, the paperboy realised that the man was completely dry, despite the heavy rain.

title: Silky
desc: A former mistress of a Duke of Argyll, this white woman has yet to leave the bedroom of this house.

title: Sliding Ashtrays
loc: Chester (Cheshire) - Coach and Horses Public House, Northgate Street
desc: Regular drinkers at the pub have seen ashtrays move themselves across tabletops and strange blue light flash from the walls.

title: Footsteps
loc: Chester (Cheshire) - Daisy and Tom Toy Shop (no longer open), Watergate Street
desc: Former staff from this store reported footsteps, the smell of pipe tobacco, something which rattled the heavy fire door, and a stock room which was blocked by a heavy table from the inside.

title: Roman
loc: Chester (Cheshire) - George and Dragon public house, 1 Liverpool Road
desc: These phantom footfalls can be heard as they take a path that now leads through several partitioned walls - it is believed to be either a single Roman centurion on guard duty, or several soldiers who march from the front of the cellar to the back.

title: Romans
desc: It is reported that the pub was built on a former Roman camp, which is why twenty Roman soldiers and an officer have been seen marching through a wall in the cellar.

title: Sarah
loc: Chester (Cheshire) - House of Bewlay Tobacconist (would become Thorntons Chocolate shop), Eastgate Street
desc: Staff would be disturbed by the sound of footsteps and a woman sobbing. Poltergeist activity would also occur; doors opened, a picture fell to the floor, and decorative studwork forcefully removed.

title: Landlord
desc: The misspelling of the pub signage is said to be due to a nineteenth century sign writer encountering the ghost of a former landlord who slit his own throat; in the worker's haste to complete the job, the man failed to spot his typographical error. Since this time, the phantom landlord has been heard gurgling in the basement.

title: Moving Beds
date: Pre-1991 (noises) and man in brown in 1976
desc: A former member of staff at the site and a colleague heard beds being moved in the ward above them, then realised the floor above was closed and empty. Another time the worker and another person heard voices and footsteps emerging from another empty ward. A man dressed in a brown suit was seen visiting his mother in 1976, although this woman later said her son had died years earlier.

title: Jack
loc: Chester (Cheshire) - Old Fire Station Restaurant, Northdate Street
desc: Sporting a beard, this phantom fireman wearing a brass helmet was known only as Jack. A fireman who watched the figure sitting on a ladder was so shocked he rang the emergency bell to summon help. Even though the phantom had vanished by the time other people arrived on the scene, the witness quit his job soon after.

title: Man in Blue Overalls
loc: Chester (Cheshire) - Old lead steel works (no longer standing)
desc: This ghost, said to be a workman who died after being hit by a train, may never be seen again: the area he haunted was scheduled for demolition and new flats will be built on the former works site.

title: Meowing
loc: Chester (Cheshire) - Overpool Road, near Charter Crescent junction
desc: Malcolm Pennicard and his car featured in the news in July after reporting a ghostly meowing coming from his car whenever he drove along Overpool Road.

title: Herbert & Charlie
loc: Chester (Cheshire) - Pepper Street garage (no longer operational, was based next to what is now Habitat)
desc: These two phantom monks were spotted several times by staff working at the garage shortly after it began opening 24 hours a day.

title: Man in Cellar
desc: The man in the cellar of this pub is said to date from the seventeenth century, while the upper part of the building is haunted by a Victorian-era maid.

title: Moving Furniture
desc: Two visitors to this property heard unexplained noises, footsteps, and furniture being moved during their stay. A window would also open and close itself.

title: Lady
loc: Chester (Cheshire) - Private residence, Newry Park area
desc: Soon after moving into this property, a phantom woman walked past one occupant, and another witness experienced a cold spot which manifested by the side of a bed. A child who walked through one room returned a few moments later to find a chair had been turned upside down.

title: Plate Thrower
loc: Chester (Cheshire) - Private residence, south-west of city centre
desc: Occupants of this property reported plates which flew from cupboards, lights turning on and off unaided, and the sound of banging and running across the landing at night. A strange female figure glimpsed at the top of the staircase which they considered 'sad'.

title: Little Girl
desc: In an area thought to be a former nursery, people are said to have their hair pulled by a phantom female child.

title: Jenny
loc: Chester (Cheshire) - River Dee, area known as The Groves
desc: Jenny is said to wait just beneath the waters of the river, waiting for an unsuspecting man to grab and drown. A Viking warrior is also reputed to haunt the same area.

title: Legionnaire
desc: This trooper walks along the walls that once protected his garrison. One legend identifies him as an officer who fell in love with a Celtic girl; one fateful day he left his post to meet her, only to let Celtic warriors enter the city and cause chaos. Some have also reported a Cavalier in the same area.

title: Squeaking Cycle
loc: Chester (Cheshire) - Saltney Junction railway station, area of
date: Early winter mornings (recurring), last seen early/mid twentieth century?
desc: The phantom bicycle with a squeaking wheel was encountered by a guard and a child in the early hours of the morning, vanishing before it reached the witnesses. The haunting reputedly began after a suicide in a nearby work area.

title: Grey Monk
desc: Heard talking in old English, this figure traditionally walks around the cathedral and made several appearances during the 1970s. On Halloween in 2003 a group of children approached the monk thinking he was a man dressed up for the occasion. When a bag was held out at him and one of the children asked, 'trick or treat', he replied 'I'll have a treat' before sticking his head into the container and eating the contents (wrappers and all).

title: Elizabeth Warburton
desc: Several ghosts are said to reside at the building, including Elizabeth Warburton, a former owner who has been spotted walking through a wall, and a man in Tudor clothing. Other entities observed consist of a Second World War Officer and a grey haired woman sitting by the piano, while bangs, children crying, and disembodied footsteps have been heard.

title: Lady in a Bonnet
desc: Wearing a white nightgown and bonnet, this phantom was observed walking through a locked door. The witness questioned their sanity before being told that others had seen the entity.

title: Sighs of Criminals
loc: Chester (Cheshire) - The Bridge of Sighs, near Northgate
desc: A man cycling to an appointment along Northgate Street looked up at the bridge and spotted two or three people dressed in old fashioned clothing. They then vanished, leaving the man rather surprised. Prisoners being led to church prior to execution would cross this bridge, and it is believed their sighs can still be heard.

title: Royalist
desc: A headless Royalist soldier is said to haunt the building where he lost his head after a cannon ball hit him during his stay. The site is also reputed to be haunted by a grey lady.

title: Lioness
desc: A reported lioness was spotted roaming the area, though a police search could find nothing.

title: Woman in Black
loc: Chester (Cheshire) - West Cheshire Hospital campus, Liverpool Road
desc: The ghostly stories concerning the woman in black who is said to haunt this site are said to go back many years. On one occasion, a guard was said to have seen the figure sitting at a desk, but when he looked again, the entity had vanished. Footsteps have also been heard walking down empty corridors.

title: Fighting Men
loc: Chester (Cheshire) - Ye Olde King's Head public house
desc: Two men, who managed to kill each other while fighting over the love of a girl, are said to remain in the upper part of this pub.
